<!-- DEFINITIONS -->
<p id="mwDQ"><b id="mwDg">Artificial intelligence</b> (<b id="mwDw">AI</b>) is the capability of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer" title="Computer" id="mwEA">computational systems</a> to perform tasks typically associated with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_intelligence" title="Human intelligence" id="mwEQ">human intelligence</a>, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning" title="Learning" id="mwEg">learning</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reason" title="Reason" id="mwEw">reasoning</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem-solving" title="Problem-solving" class="mw-redirect" id="mwFA">problem-solving</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception" title="Perception" id="mwFQ">perception</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision-making" title="Decision-making" id="mwFg">decision-making</a>. It is a field of research in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering" title="Engineering" id="mwFw">engineering</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics" title="Mathematics" id="mwGA">mathematics</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science" title="Computer science" id="mwGQ">computer science</a> that develops and studies methods and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software" title="Software" id="mwGg">software</a> that enable machines to perceive their environment and use <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mwGw">learning</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence" title="Intelligence" id="mwHA">intelligence</a> to take actions that maximise their chances of achieving defined goals.<sup about="#mwt12" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4_1-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4-1&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1–4&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4-1" id="mwHQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwHg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHw">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- APPLICATIONS -->
<p id="mwIQ">High-profile <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applications_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Applications of artificial intelligence" id="mwIg">applications of AI</a> include advanced <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_search_engine" title="Web search engine" class="mw-redirect" id="mwIw">web search engines</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot" title="Chatbot" id="mwJA">chatbots</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_assistant" title="Virtual assistant" id="mwJQ">virtual assistants</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_vehicles" title="Autonomous vehicles" class="mw-redirect" id="mwJg">autonomous vehicles</a>, play and analysis in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_game" title="Strategy game" id="mwJw">strategy games</a> (e.g., <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess" title="Chess" id="mwKA">chess</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(game)" title="Go (game)" id="mwKQ">Go</a>), and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI" title="Generative AI" id="mwKg">content generation</a> (e.g. images, audio, and videos).</p>

<!-- GOALS AND TOOLS: SCOPE OF AI -->
<p id="mwKw">The traditional goals of AI research include learning, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_reasoning" title="Automated reasoning" id="mwLA">reasoning</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_representation" title="Knowledge representation" class="mw-redirect" id="mwLQ">knowledge representation</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_planning_and_scheduling" title="Automated planning and scheduling" id="mwLg">planning</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing" title="Natural language processing" id="mwLw">natural language processing</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_perception" title="Machine perception" id="mwMA">perception</a>, as well as support for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotics" title="Robotics" id="mwMQ">robotics</a>.<sup about="#mwt15" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Problems_of_AI_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" these goals, AI researchers use techniques including <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_search" title="State space search" class="mw-redirect" id="mwNg">state space id="cite_ref-Tools_of_AI_3-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Tools of <!-- HISTORY AND ETHICS -->
<p id="mwUg">Artificial intelligence was founded as an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_discipline" title="Academic discipline" id="mwUw">academic discipline</a> in 1956.<sup about="#mwt29" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Dartmouth_workshop_6-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Dartmouth workshop&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Dartmouth_workshop-6" id="mwVA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwVQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVg">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVw">]</span></span></a></sup> The field went through multiple cycles of optimism throughout <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_artificial_intelligence" title="History of artificial intelligence" id="mwWA">its history</a>,<sup about="#mwt30" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Succ1_7-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Succ1&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Succ1-7" id="mwWQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwWg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWw">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt31" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Fund01_8-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Fund01&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Fund01-8" id="mwXQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwXg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXw">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwYA">]</span></span></a></sup> followed by periods of disappointment and loss of funding, known as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_winter" title="AI winter" id="mwYQ">AI winters</a>.<sup about="#mwt32" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-First_AI_Winter_9-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;First AI Winter&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-First_AI_Winter-9" id="mwYg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwYw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZA">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt33" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Second_AI_Winter_10-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Second AI Winter&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Second_AI_Winter-10" id="mwZg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwZw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaA">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Funding and interest increased substantially after 2012, when <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit" title="Graphics processing unit" id="mwag">graphics processing units</a> (GPUs) started being used to accelerate neural networks, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning" title="Deep learning" id="mwaw">deep learning</a> outperformed previous AI techniques.<sup about="#mwt34" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Deep_learning_revolution_11-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Deep learning revolution&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Deep_learning_revolution-11" id="mwbA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwbQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbg">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbw">]</span></span></a></sup> This growth accelerated further after 2017 with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_architecture" title="Transformer architecture" class="mw-redirect" id="mwcA">transformer architecture</a>.<sup about="#mwt26" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEToews2023_12-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEToews2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEToews2023-12&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Toews&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEToews2023-12" id="mwcQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwcg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcw">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwdA">]</span></span></a></sup> In the 2020s, an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_boom" title="AI boom" id="mwdQ">AI boom</a> coincided with advances in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI" title="Generative AI" id="mwdg">generative AI</a>, which became widespread and allowed for the creation and modification of media. In addition to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_safety" title="AI safety" id="mwdw">AI safety</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI#Concerns" title="Generative AI" id="mweA">unintended consequences and harms</a> from the use of AI, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethics_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Ethics of artificial intelligence" id="mweQ">ethical concerns</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_aftermath_scenarios" title="AI aftermath scenarios" id="mweg">AI's long-term effects</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_impacts_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Environmental impacts of artificial intelligence" class="mw-redirect" id="mwew">environmental effects</a>,<sup about="#mwt35" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-UN_13-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;UN&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-UN-13" id="mwfA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwfQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfg">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfw">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Existential_risk_from_artificial_intelligence" title="Existential risk from artificial intelligence" id="mwgA">potential existential risks</a> have prompted discussions of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Regulation of artificial intelligence" id="mwgQ">AI regulation</a>.</p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwgg" data-mw="{&quot;autoGenerated&quot;:true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwgw" aria-labelledby="Goals"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Goals">Goals</h2></div>
<p id="mwhA">The general problem of simulating (or creating) intelligence has been broken down into subproblems. These consist of specific traits or capabilities that researchers expect an intelligent system to display. The traits described below have received the most attention and cover the scope of AI research.<sup about="#mwt36" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Problems_of_AI_2-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Problems of AI&quot;,&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;html&quot;:&quot;&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;\&quot;Problems of AI\&quot;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-Problems_of_AI-2" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwhQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwhg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwhw">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwiA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwiQ" aria-labelledby="Reasoning_and_problem-solving"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Reasoning_and_problem-solving">Reasoning and problem-solving</h3></div>
<p id="mwig">Early researchers developed algorithms that imitated step-by-step reasoning that humans use when solving puzzles or making logical <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deductive_reasoning" title="Deductive reasoning" id="mwiw">deductions</a>.<sup about="#mwt44" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-14&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-14" id="mwjA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwjQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjg">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjw">]</span></span></a></sup> By the late 1980s and 1990s, methods were developed for dealing with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncertainty" title="Uncertainty" id="mwkA">uncertain</a> or incomplete information, employing concepts from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability" title="Probability" id="mwkQ">probability</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics" title="Economics" id="mwkg">economics</a>.<sup about="#mwt49" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-15" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-15&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-15" id="mwkw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwlA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwlQ">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwlg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwlw">Many of these <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm" title="Algorithm" id="mwmA">algorithms</a> were insufficient for solving large reasoning problems because they experienced a "combinatorial explosion", meaning they become exponentially slower as the problems grow.<sup about="#mwt51" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Intractability_and_efficiency_and_the_combinatorial_explosion_16-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Intractability and efficiency and the combinatorial explosion&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Intractability_and_efficiency_and_the_combinatorial_explosion-16&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Intractability_and_efficiency_and_the_combinatorial_explosion-16" id="mwmQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwmg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwmw">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnA">]</span></span></a></sup> Even humans rarely use the step-by-step deduction that early AI research could model. Humans solve most of their problems using fast, intuitive judgments.<sup about="#mwt56" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Psychological_evidence_of_the_prevalence_of_sub_17-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Psychological evidence of the prevalence of sub&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Psychological_evidence_of_the_prevalence_of_sub-17&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Psychological_evidence_of_the_prevalence_of_sub-17" id="mwnQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwng"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnw">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwoA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwoQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reasoning_model" title="Reasoning model" id="mwog">Reasoning models</a>, a type of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model" title="Large language model" id="mwow">large language model</a> (LLM) trained to generate intermediate chains-of-thought, emerged in 2024 and allowed improved performance on complex problems in mathematics and coding.<sup about="#mwt59" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-18" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-18&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-18" id="mwpA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwpQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpg">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpw">]</span></span></a></sup> These models can produce incorrect outputs or "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallucination_(artificial_intelligence)" title="Hallucination (artificial intelligence)" id="mwqA">hallucinations</a>," unlike symbolic <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reasoning_system" title="Reasoning system" id="mwqQ">reasoning systems</a>.<sup about="#mwt62" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Garcez_19-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Garcez&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Garcez-19&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Garcez-19" id="mwqg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwqw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwrA">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwrQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwrg" aria-labelledby="Knowledge_representation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Knowledge_representation">Knowledge representation</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwrw"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:General_Formal_Ontology.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwsA"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:General_Formal_Ontology.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/General_Formal_Ontology.svg/330px-General_Formal_Ontology.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/General_Formal_Ontology.svg/960px-General_Formal_Ontology.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="512" data-file-height="512" data-file-type="drawing" height="300" width="300" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.2" id="mwsQ"></a><figcaption id="mwsg">An ontology represents knowledge as a set of concepts within a domain and the relationships between those concepts.</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwsw">AI programs use knowledge to answer questions intelligently and make deductions about real-world facts.</p>

<p id="mwtA">Formal <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_representation" title="Knowledge representation" class="mw-redirect" id="mwtQ">knowledge representation</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_engineering" title="Knowledge engineering" id="mwtg">knowledge engineering</a> use <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_AI" title="Symbolic AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwtw">symbols</a> to represent words, concepts and things in the world.<sup about="#mwt120" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-20" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-20&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-20" id="mwuA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwuQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwug">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwuw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt63" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-26" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-26&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Formal knowledge representations are used in content-based indexing and retrieval,{{Sfnp|Smoliar|Zhang|1994}} scene interpretation,{{Sfnp|Neumann|Möller|2008}} clinical decision support,{{Sfnp|Kuperman|Reichley|Bailey|2006}} knowledge discovery (mining \&quot;interesting\&quot; and actionable inferences from large [[database]]s),{{Sfnp|McGarry|2005}} and other areas.{{Sfnp|Bertini|Del Bimbo|Torniai|2006}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-26" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwvA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwvQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvg">[</span>c<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwvw">]</span></span></a></sup> A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_base" title="Knowledge base" id="mwwA">knowledge base</a> is a body of knowledge represented in a form that can be used by a program. An <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontology_(information_science)" title="Ontology (information science)" id="mwwQ">ontology</a> is the set of objects, relations, concepts, and properties used by a particular domain of knowledge.<sup about="#mwt81" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021272_27-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021272&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021272-27&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;272&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021272-27" id="mwwg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwww"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwxA">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwxQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Formal knowledge has been studied extensively since the 1970s and researchers have developed formalisms for a wide variety of difficult domains.<sup about="#mwt84" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-33" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" <p id="mwyg">The symbolic approach has difficulty with several problems: the breadth of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonsense_knowledge" title="Commonsense knowledge" class="mw-redirect" id="mwyw">commonsense knowledge</a> (the set of atomic facts the average person knows is enormous),<sup about="#mwt134" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Breadth_of_commonsense_knowledge_34-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Breadth of commonsense knowledge&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Breadth_of_commonsense_knowledge-34&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Breadth_of_commonsense_knowledge-34" id="mwzA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwzQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzg">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzw">]</span></span></a></sup> the sub-symbolic form of most commonsense knowledge (much of what people know is not represented as "facts" or "statements" they can express verbally),<sup about="#mwt135" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Psychological_evidence_of_the_prevalence_of_sub_17-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Psychological evidence of the prevalence of sub&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Psychological_evidence_of_the_prevalence_of_sub-17" id="mw0A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw0Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0g">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0w">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_acquisition" title="Knowledge acquisition" id="mw1A">knowledge acquisition</a> (the problem of obtaining knowledge for AI applications).<sup about="#mwt121" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-37" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-37&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Knowledge acquistion is among the reasons that [[expert system]]s proved to be inefficient for capturing knowledge.{{Sfnp|Newquist|1994|p=296}}{{Sfnp|Crevier|1993|pp=204–208}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-37" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mw1Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw1g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw1w">[</span>e<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw2A">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw2Q"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_models" title="Large language models" class="mw-redirect" id="mw2g">Large language models</a> (and some other AI programs developed since 2012) do not require explicit, symbolic knowledge. They acquire knowledge by being trained on the combined text of millions of books and billions of websites. Modern AI can also learn about a domain by running experiments (as when <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlphaZero" title="AlphaZero" id="mw2w">AlphaZero</a> learns game strategy by playing against itself). <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mw3A">Machine learning</a> solves the problems of general knowledge, commonsense knowledge and knowledge acquisition, however this approach has struggled with accurate recall and valid reasoning.<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt136" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mw3Q" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;citation needed&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Citation_needed&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;date&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;August 2026&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_August_2026" about="#mwt136"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt136" id="mw3g"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (August 2026)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mw3w" aria-labelledby="Planning_and_decision-making"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Planning_and_decision-making">Planning and decision-making</h3></div>
<p id="mw4A">An "agent" is any entity (artificial or not) that perceives and takes actions in the world. A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rational_agent" title="Rational agent" id="mw4Q">rational agent</a> has goals or preferences and takes actions to make them happen.<sup about="#mwt137" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-38" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-38&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;\&quot;Rational agent\&quot; is general term used in [[economics]], [[philosophy]] and theoretical artificial intelligence. It can refer to anything that directs its behaviour to accomplish goals, such as a person, an animal, a corporation, a nation, or in the case of AI, a computer program.\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-38" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mw4g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw4w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5A">[</span>f<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5Q">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt140" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021528_39-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021528&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021528-39&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;528&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021528-39" id="mw5g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw5w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw6A">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw6Q">]</span></span></a></sup> In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_planning" title="Automated planning" class="mw-redirect" id="mw6g">automated planning</a>, the agent has a specific goal.<sup about="#mwt144" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-40" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-40&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-40" id="mw6w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw7A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7Q">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7g">]</span></span></a></sup> In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_decision-making" title="Automated decision-making" id="mw7w">automated decision-making</a>, the agent has preferences—there are some situations it would prefer to be in, and some situations it is trying to avoid. The decision-making agent assigns a number to each situation (called its "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utility" title="Utility" id="mw8A">utility</a>") that measures how much the agent prefers it. For each possible action, it can calculate the "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_utility" title="Expected utility" class="mw-redirect" id="mw8Q">expected utility</a>": the utility of all possible outcomes of the action, weighted by the probability that the outcome will occur. It can then choose the action with the maximum expected utility.<sup about="#mwt146" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-41" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-41&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-41" id="mw8g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw8w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw9A">[</span>35<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw9Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mw9g">In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_planning_and_scheduling#classical_planning" title="Automated planning and scheduling" id="mw9w">classical planning</a>, the agent knows exactly what the effect of any action will be.<sup about="#mwt148" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-42" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-42&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-42" id="mw-A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw-Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-g">[</span>36<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw-w">]</span></span></a></sup> In most real-world problems, however, the agent may not be certain about the situation it is in (it is "unknown" or "unobservable") and it may not know for certain what will happen after each possible action (it is not "deterministic"). It must choose an action by making a probabilistic guess and then reassess the situation to see if the action worked.<sup about="#mwt150" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-43" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-43&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-43" id="mw_A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw_Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw_g">[</span>37<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw_w">]</span></span></a></sup></p> 

<p id="mwAQA">Alongside thorough testing and improvement based on previous decisions, having an explanation for why the agent took certain decisions is a way to build trust, especially when the decisions have to be relied upon.<sup about="#mwt152" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-44" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-44&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-44" id="mwAQE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQM">[</span>38<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAQU">In some problems, the agent's preferences may be uncertain, especially if there are other agents or humans involved. These preferences may be learned (e.g., with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_reinforcement_learning" title="Inverse reinforcement learning" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAQY">inverse reinforcement learning</a>), or the agent can seek information to improve them.<sup about="#mwt155" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-45" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-45&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-45" id="mwAQc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQk">[</span>39<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQo">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_value_theory" title="Information value theory" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAQs">Information value theory</a> can be used to weigh the value of exploratory or experimental actions.<sup about="#mwt157" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-46" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-46&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-46" id="mwAQw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAQ0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQ4">[</span>40<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAQ8">]</span></span></a></sup> The space of possible future actions and situations is typically <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intractably" title="Intractably" class="mw-redirect" id="mwARA">intractably</a> large, so the agents must take actions and evaluate situations while being uncertain of the outcome.</p>

<p id="mwARE">A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_decision_process" title="Markov decision process" id="mwARI">Markov decision process</a> has a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finite-state_machine" title="Finite-state machine" id="mwARM">transition model</a> that describes the probability that a particular action will change the state in a particular way and a reward function that supplies the utility of each state and the cost of each action. A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinforcement_learning#Policy" title="Reinforcement learning" id="mwARQ">policy</a> associates a decision with each possible state. The policy could be calculated (e.g., by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Policy_iteration" title="Policy iteration" class="mw-redirect" id="mwARU">policy iteration</a>), determined by a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heuristic" title="Heuristic" id="mwARY">heuristic</a>, or learned.<sup about="#mwt159" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-47" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-47&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-47" id="mwARc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwARg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARk">[</span>41<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwARo">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwARs"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory" title="Game theory" id="mwARw">Game theory</a> describes the rational behaviour of multiple interacting agents and is used in AI programs that make decisions involving other agents.<sup about="#mwt161" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-48" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-48&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-48" id="mwAR0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAR4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAR8">[</span>42<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwASE" aria-labelledby="Learning"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Learning">Learning</h3></div>
<p id="mwASI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mwASM">Machine learning</a> is the study of programs that can improve their performance on a given task automatically.<sup about="#mwt175" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-49" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-49&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-49" id="mwASQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwASU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASY">[</span>43<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASc">]</span></span></a></sup> It has been a part of AI from the beginning.<sup about="#mwt162" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-52" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-52&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Alan Turing]] discussed the centrality of learning as early as 1950, in his classic paper \&quot;[[Computing Machinery and Intelligence]]\&quot;.{{Sfnp|Turing|1950}} In 1956, at the original Dartmouth AI summer conference, [[Ray Solomonoff]] wrote a report on unsupervised probabilistic machine learning: \&quot;An Inductive Inference Machine\&quot;.{{Sfnp|Solomonoff|1956}}\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-52" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwASg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwASk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASo">[</span>g<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwASs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwASw"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Supervised_and_unsupervised_learning.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwAS0"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Supervised_and_unsupervised_learning.png" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Supervised_and_unsupervised_learning.png/500px-Supervised_and_unsupervised_learning.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4d/Supervised_and_unsupervised_learning.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled 2x" data-file-width="681" data-file-height="308" data-file-type="bitmap" height="158" width="350" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.4" id="mwAS4"></a><figcaption id="mwAS8">In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supervised_learning" title="Supervised learning" id="mwATA">supervised learning</a>, the training data is labelled with the expected answers, while in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsupervised_learning" title="Unsupervised learning" id="mwATE">unsupervised learning</a>, the model identifies patterns or structures in unlabelled data.</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwATI">There are several kinds of machine learning: </p>

<ul id="mwATM"><li id="mwATQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsupervised_learning" title="Unsupervised learning" id="mwATU">Unsupervised learning</a> analyses a stream of data, finds patterns, and makes predictions without any other guidance.<sup about="#mwt179" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-53" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-53&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-53" id="mwATY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwATc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATg">[</span>46<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwATk">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwATo"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supervised_learning" title="Supervised learning" id="mwATs">Supervised learning</a> requires labelling the training data with the expected answers, and comes in two main varieties: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_classification" title="Statistical classification" id="mwATw">classification</a> (where the program must learn to predict what category the input belongs in) and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regression_analysis" title="Regression analysis" id="mwAT0">regression</a> (where the program must deduce a numeric function based on numeric input).<sup about="#mwt182" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Supervised_learning_54-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Supervised learning&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Supervised_learning-54&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Supervised_learning-54" id="mwAT4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAT8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUA">[</span>47<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUE">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwAUI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinforcement_learning" title="Reinforcement learning" id="mwAUM">Reinforcement learning</a> is when the agent is rewarded for good responses and punished for bad ones. The agent learns to choose responses that are classified as "good".<sup about="#mwt185" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-55" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-55&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-55" id="mwAUQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAUU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUY">[</span>48<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUc">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwAUg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_learning" title="Transfer learning" id="mwAUk">Transfer learning</a> is when the knowledge gained from one problem is applied to a new problem.<sup about="#mwt188" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-56" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-56&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-56" id="mwAUo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAUs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAUw">[</span>49<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAU0">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwAU4"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning" title="Deep learning" id="mwAU8">Deep learning</a> is a type of machine learning that runs inputs through biologically inspired <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_networks" title="Artificial neural networks" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAVA">artificial neural networks</a> for all of these types of learning.<sup about="#mwt191" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-57" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-57&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-57" id="mwAVE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAVI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVM">[</span>50<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVQ">]</span></span></a></sup></li></ul>

<p id="mwAVU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_learning_theory" title="Computational learning theory" id="mwAVY">Computational learning theory</a> can assess learners by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_complexity" title="Computational complexity" id="mwAVc">computational complexity</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sample_complexity" title="Sample complexity" id="mwAVg">sample complexity</a> (how much data is required), or other notions of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimization" title="Optimization" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAVk">optimisation</a>.<sup about="#mwt194" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-58" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-58&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-58" id="mwAVo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAVs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAVw">[</span>51<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAV0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<div style="clear:both;" class="" about="#mwt195" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwAV4" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Clear&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Clear&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"></div>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="6" id="mwAV8" aria-labelledby="Natural_language_processing"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Natural_language_processing">Natural language processing</h3></div>
<p id="mwAWA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing" title="Natural language processing" id="mwAWE">Natural language processing</a> (NLP) allows programs to read, write, and communicate in human languages.<sup about="#mwt199" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-59" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-59&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-59" id="mwAWI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAWM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAWQ">[</span>52<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAWU">]</span></span></a></sup> Specific problems include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_recognition" title="Speech recognition" id="mwAWY">speech recognition</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_synthesis" title="Speech synthesis" id="mwAWc">speech synthesis</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_translation" title="Machine translation" id="mwAWg">machine translation</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_extraction" title="Information extraction" id="mwAWk">information extraction</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_retrieval" title="Information retrieval" id="mwAWo">information retrieval</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Question_answering" title="Question answering" id="mwAWs">question answering</a>.<sup about="#mwt201" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-60" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-60&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-60" id="mwAWw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAW0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAW4">[</span>53<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAW8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAXA">Early work, based on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noam_Chomsky" title="Noam Chomsky" id="mwAXE">Noam Chomsky</a>'s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_grammar" title="Generative grammar" id="mwAXI">generative grammar</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_network" title="Semantic network" id="mwAXM">semantic networks</a>, had difficulty with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word-sense_disambiguation" title="Word-sense disambiguation" id="mwAXQ">word-sense disambiguation</a><sup about="#mwt202" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-61" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-61&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See {{Section link|AI winter|Machine translation and the ALPAC report of 1966\n}}.&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-61" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwAXU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAXY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAXc">[</span>h<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAXg">]</span></span></a></sup> unless restricted to small domains called "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blocks_world" title="Blocks world" id="mwAXk">micro-worlds</a>" (due to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonsense_knowledge_(artificial_intelligence)" title="Commonsense knowledge (artificial intelligence)" id="mwAXo">common sense knowledge problem</a><sup about="#mwt205" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Breadth_of_commonsense_knowledge_34-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Breadth of commonsense knowledge&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Breadth_of_commonsense_knowledge-34" id="mwAXs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAXw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAX0">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAX4">]</span></span></a></sup>). British <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguist" title="Linguist" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAX8">linguist</a> and philosopher <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Masterman" title="Margaret Masterman" id="mwAYA">Margaret Masterman</a> believed it was meaning and not grammar that was the key to understanding languages,<sup about="#mwt208" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-62" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-62&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-62" id="mwAYE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAYI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYM">[</span>54<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYQ">]</span></span></a></sup> and that dictionaries and especially <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thesauri" title="Thesauri" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAYU">thesauri</a> should be the basis of computational language structure.<sup about="#mwt211" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-63" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-63&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-63" id="mwAYY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAYc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYg">[</span>55<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAYk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAYo">Modern deep learning techniques for NLP include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_embedding" title="Word embedding" id="mwAYs">word embedding</a> (representing words, typically as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_space" title="Vector space" id="mwAYw">vectors</a> encoding their meaning),<sup about="#mwt212" </section><section data-mw-section-id="7" id="mwAas" aria-labelledby="Perception"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Perception">Perception</h3></div>

<p id="mwAaw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_perception" title="Machine perception" id="mwAa0">Machine perception</a> is the ability to use input from sensors (such as cameras, microphones, wireless signals, active <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lidar" title="Lidar" id="mwAa4">lidar</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonar" title="Sonar" id="mwAa8">sonar</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radar" title="Radar" id="mwAbA">radar</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tactile_sensor" title="Tactile sensor" id="mwAbE">tactile sensors</a>) to deduce aspects of the world. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_vision" title="Computer vision" id="mwAbI">Computer vision</a> is the ability to analyse visual input.<sup about="#mwt232" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-70" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-70&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-70" id="mwAbM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAbQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAbU">[</span>62<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAbY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="8" id="mwAdI" aria-labelledby="Social_intelligence"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Social_intelligence">Social intelligence</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwAdM"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kismet-IMG_6007-gradient.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwAdQ"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kismet-IMG_6007-gradient.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Kismet-IMG_6007-gradient.jpg/250px-Kismet-IMG_6007-gradient.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Kismet-IMG_6007-gradient.jpg/500px-Kismet-IMG_6007-gradient.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="5500" data-file-height="3667" data-file-type="bitmap" height="167" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwAdU"></a><figcaption id="mwAdY"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kismet_(robot)" title="Kismet (robot)" id="mwAdc">Kismet</a>, a robot head made in the 1990s, is a machine that can recognise and simulate emotions.<sup about="#mwt248" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMIT_AIL2014_76-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMIT AIL2014&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMIT_AIL2014-76&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;MIT AIL&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2014&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMIT_AIL2014-76" id="mwAdg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAdk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAdo">[</span>68<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAds">]</span></span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwAdw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affective_computing" title="Affective computing" id="mwAd0">Affective computing</a> is a field that comprises systems that recognise, interpret, process, or simulate human <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affect_(psychology)" title="Affect (psychology)" id="mwAd4">affect</a> (feeling, emotion, and mood).<sup about="#mwt255" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-77" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-77&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-77" id="mwAd8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAeA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAeE">[</span>69<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAeI">]</span></span></a></sup> For example, some <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_assistant" title="Virtual assistant" id="mwAeM">virtual assistants</a> are programmed to speak conversationally or even banter humorously; it makes them appear more sensitive to the emotional dynamics of human interaction, or to otherwise facilitate <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human–computer_interaction" title="Human–computer interaction" id="mwAeQ">human–computer interaction</a>.</p>

<p id="mwAeU">However, this tends to give naïve users an unrealistic conception of the intelligence of existing computer agents.<sup about="#mwt256" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWaddell2018_78-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEWaddell2018&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEWaddell2018-78&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Waddell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2018&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWaddell2018-78" id="mwAeY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAec"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAeg">[</span>70<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAek">]</span></span></a></sup> Moderate successes related to affective computing include textual <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentiment_analysis" title="Sentiment analysis" id="mwAeo">sentiment analysis</a> and, more recently, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimodal_sentiment_analysis" title="Multimodal sentiment analysis" id="mwAes">multimodal sentiment analysis</a>, wherein AI classifies the effects displayed by a videotaped subject.<sup about="#mwt259" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPoriaCambriaBajpaiHussain2017_79-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEPoriaCambriaBajpaiHussain2017&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEPoriaCambriaBajpaiHussain2017-79&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Poria&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Cambria&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Bajpai &quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hussain&quot;},&quot;5&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2017&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPoriaCambriaBajpaiHussain2017-79" id="mwAew"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAe0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAe4">[</span>71<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAe8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="9" id="mwAfA" aria-labelledby="General_intelligence"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="General_intelligence">General intelligence</h3></div>

<p id="mwAfE">A machine with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence" title="Artificial general intelligence" id="mwAfI">artificial general intelligence</a> (AGI) would be able to solve a wide variety of problems with breadth and versatility similar to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_intelligence" title="Human intelligence" id="mwAfM">human intelligence</a>.<sup about="#mwt267" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Artificial_general_intelligence_80-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Artificial general intelligence&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Artificial_general_intelligence-80&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Artificial_general_intelligence-80" id="mwAfQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAfU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAfY">[</span>72<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAfc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="10" id="mwAfg" aria-labelledby="Techniques"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Techniques">Techniques</h2></div>
<p id="mwAfk">AI research uses a wide variety of techniques to accomplish the goals above.<sup about="#mwt268" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Tools_of_AI_3-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Tools of AI&quot;,&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Tools_of_AI-3&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;\&quot;Tools of AI\&quot;&quot;},&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;This list of tools is based on the topics covered by the major AI textbooks, including: {{Harvtxt|Russell|Norvig|2021}}, {{Harvtxt|Luger|Stubblefield|2004}}, {{Harvtxt|Poole|Mackworth|Goebel|1998}} and {{Harvtxt|Nilsson|1998}}.&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-Tools_of_AI-3" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwAfo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAfs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAfw">[</span>b<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAf0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="11" id="mwAf4" aria-labelledby="Search_and_optimisation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Search_and_optimisation">Search and optimisation</h3></div>
<p id="mwAf8">There are two different kinds of search used in AI: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_search" title="State space search" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAgA">state space search</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_search_(optimization)" title="Local search (optimization)" id="mwAgE">local search</a>:</p>

<section data-mw-section-id="12" id="mwAgI" aria-labelledby="State_space_search"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="State_space_search">State space search</h4></div>
<p id="mwAgM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_search" title="State space search" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAgQ">State space search</a> searches through a tree of possible states to try to find a goal state.<sup about="#mwt275" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-81" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-81&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-81" id="mwAgU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAgY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAgc">[</span>73<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAgg">]</span></span></a></sup> For example, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_planning_and_scheduling" title="Automated planning and scheduling" id="mwAgk">planning</a> algorithms search through trees of goals and subgoals, attempting to find a path to a target goal, a process called <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Means-ends_analysis" title="Means-ends analysis" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAgo">means-ends analysis</a>.<sup about="#mwt271" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021sect._11.2_82-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021sect. 11.2&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021sect._11.2-82&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;loc&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sect. 11.2&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021sect._11.2-82" id="mwAgs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAgw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAg0">[</span>74<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAg4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAg8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brute_force_search" title="Brute force search" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAhA">Simple exhaustive searches</a><sup about="#mwt280" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-83" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-83&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-83" id="mwAhE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAhI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAhM">[</span>75<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAhQ">]</span></span></a></sup> are rarely sufficient for most real-world problems: the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_algorithm" title="Search algorithm" id="mwAhU">search space</a> (the number of places to search) quickly grows to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronomically_large" title="Astronomically large" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAhY">astronomical numbers</a>. The result is a search that is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computation_time" title="Computation time" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAhc">too slow</a> or never completes.<sup about="#mwt281" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Intractability_and_efficiency_and_the_combinatorial_explosion_16-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Intractability and efficiency and the combinatorial explosion&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Intractability_and_efficiency_and_the_combinatorial_explosion-16" id="mwAhg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAhk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAho">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAhs">]</span></span></a></sup> "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heuristics" title="Heuristics" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAhw">Heuristics</a>" or "rules of thumb" can help prioritise choices that are more likely to reach a goal.<sup about="#mwt286" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-84" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-84&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-84" id="mwAh0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAh4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAh8">[</span>76<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAiA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAiE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adversarial_search" title="Adversarial search" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAiI">Adversarial search</a> is used for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_AI" title="Game AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAiM">game-playing</a> programs, such as chess or Go. It searches through a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_tree" title="Game tree" id="mwAiQ">tree</a> of possible moves and countermoves, looking for a winning position.<sup about="#mwt288" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-85" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-85&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-85" id="mwAiU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAiY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAic">[</span>77<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAig">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="13" id="mwAik" aria-labelledby="Local_search"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Local_search">Local search</h4></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size skin-invert-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwAio"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gradient_descent.gif" class="mw-file-description" id="mwAis"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gradient_descent.gif" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Gradient_descent.gif/330px-Gradient_descent.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a3/Gradient_descent.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled 2x" data-file-width="360" data-file-height="292" data-file-type="bitmap" height="243" width="300" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.2" id="mwAiw"></a><figcaption id="mwAi0">Illustration of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent" title="Gradient descent" id="mwAi4">gradient descent</a> for three different starting points; two parameters (represented by the plan coordinates) are adjusted in order to minimise the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loss_function" title="Loss function" id="mwAi8">loss function</a> (the height).</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwAjA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_search_(optimization)" title="Local search (optimization)" id="mwAjE">Local search</a> uses <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_optimization" title="Mathematical optimization" id="mwAjI">mathematical optimisation</a> to find a solution to a problem. It begins with some form of guess and refines it incrementally.<sup about="#mwt290" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-86" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-86&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-86" id="mwAjM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAjQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAjU">[</span>78<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAjY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAjc"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent" title="Gradient descent" id="mwAjg">Gradient descent</a> is a type of local search that optimises a set of numerical parameters by incrementally adjusting them to minimise a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loss_function" title="Loss function" id="mwAjk">loss function</a>. Variants of gradient descent are commonly used to train <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_network" title="Artificial neural network" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAjo">neural networks</a>,<sup about="#mwt293" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-87" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-87&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-87" id="mwAjs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAjw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAj0">[</span>79<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAj4">]</span></span></a></sup> through the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backpropagation" title="Backpropagation" id="mwAj8">backpropagation</a> algorithm.</p>

<p id="mwAkA">Another type of local search is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_computation" title="Evolutionary computation" id="mwAkE">evolutionary computation</a>, which aims to iteratively improve a set of candidate solutions by "mutating" and "recombining" them, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_selection" title="Artificial selection" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAkI">selecting</a> only the fittest to survive each generation.<sup about="#mwt295" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-88" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-88&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-88" id="mwAkM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAkQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAkU">[</span>80<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAkY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAkc">Distributed search processes can coordinate via <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swarm_intelligence" title="Swarm intelligence" id="mwAkg">swarm intelligence</a> algorithms. Two popular swarm algorithms used in search are <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_swarm_optimization" title="Particle swarm optimization" id="mwAkk">particle swarm optimisation</a> (inspired by bird <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flocking" title="Flocking" id="mwAko">flocking</a>) and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant_colony_optimization" title="Ant colony optimization" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAks">art colony optimisation</a> (inspired by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant_trail" title="Ant trail" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAkw">ant trails</a>).<sup about="#mwt296" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMerkleMiddendorf2013_89-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMerkleMiddendorf2013&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMerkleMiddendorf2013-89&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Merkle&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Middendorf&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2013&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMerkleMiddendorf2013-89" id="mwAk0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAk4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAk8">[</span>81<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAlA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="14" id="mwAlE" aria-labelledby="Logic"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Logic">Logic</h3></div>
<p id="mwAlI">Formal <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic" title="Logic" id="mwAlM">logic</a> is used for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_reasoning" title="Automatic reasoning" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAlQ">reasoning</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_representation" title="Knowledge representation" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAlU">knowledge representation</a>.<sup about="#mwt302" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-90" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-90&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-90" id="mwAlY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAlc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAlg">[</span>82<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAlk">]</span></span></a></sup>
