Formal logic comes in two main forms: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propositional_logic" title="Propositional logic" id="mwAlo">propositional logic</a> (which operates on statements that are true or false and uses <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logical_connective" title="Logical connective" id="mwAls">logical connectives</a> such as "and", "or", "not" and "implies")<sup about="#mwt306" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-91" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-91&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-91" id="mwAlw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAl0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAl4">[</span>83<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAl8">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predicate_logic" title="Predicate logic" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAmA">predicate logic</a> (which also operates on objects, predicates and relations and uses <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantifier_(logic)" title="Quantifier (logic)" id="mwAmE">quantifiers</a> such as "<i id="mwAmI">Every</i> <i id="mwAmM">X</i> is a <i id="mwAmQ">Y</i>" and "There are <i id="mwAmU">some</i> <i id="mwAmY">X</i>s that are <i id="mwAmc">Y</i>s").<sup about="#mwt311" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-92" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-92&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-92" id="mwAmg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAmk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAmo">[</span>84<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAms">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAmw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deductive_reasoning" title="Deductive reasoning" id="mwAm0">Deductive reasoning</a> in logic is the process of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logical_proof" title="Logical proof" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAm4">proving</a> a new statement (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logical_consequence" title="Logical consequence" id="mwAm8">conclusion</a>) from other statements that are given and assumed to be true (the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premise" title="Premise" id="mwAnA">premises</a>).<sup about="#mwt313" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-93" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-93&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-93" id="mwAnE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAnI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAnM">[</span>85<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAnQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Proofs can be structured as proof <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_structure" title="Tree structure" id="mwAnU">trees</a>, in which nodes are labelled by sentences, and children nodes are connected to parent nodes by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inference_rule" title="Inference rule" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAnY">inference rules</a>.</p>

<p id="mwAnc">Given a problem and a set of premises, problem-solving reduces to searching for a proof tree whose root node is labelled by a solution of the problem and whose <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_nodes" title="Leaf nodes" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAng">leaf nodes</a> are labelled by premises or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axiom" title="Axiom" id="mwAnk">axioms</a>. In the case of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_clause" title="Horn clause" id="mwAno">Horn clauses</a>, problem-solving search can be performed by reasoning <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_chaining" title="Forward chaining" id="mwAns">forwards</a> from the premises or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backward_chaining" title="Backward chaining" id="mwAnw">backwards</a> from the problem.<sup about="#mwt318" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-94" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-94&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-94" id="mwAn0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAn4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAn8">[</span>86<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAoA">]</span></span></a></sup> In the more general case of the clausal form of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-order_logic" title="First-order logic" id="mwAoE">first-order logic</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resolution_(logic)" title="Resolution (logic)" id="mwAoI">resolution</a> is a single, axiom-free rule of inference, in which a problem is solved by proving a contradiction from premises that include the negation of the problem to be solved.<sup about="#mwt320" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-95" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-95&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-95" id="mwAoM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAoQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAoU">[</span>87<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAoY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAoc">Inference in both Horn clause logic and first-order logic is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undecidable_problem" title="Undecidable problem" id="mwAog">undecidable</a>, and therefore <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intractable_problem" title="Intractable problem" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAok">intractable</a>. However, backward reasoning with Horn clauses, which underpins computation in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic_programming" title="Logic programming" id="mwAoo">logic programming</a> language <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prolog" title="Prolog" id="mwAos">Prolog</a>, is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_complete" title="Turing complete" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAow">Turing complete</a>. Moreover, its efficiency is competitive with computation in other <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_programming" title="Symbolic programming" id="mwAo0">symbolic programming</a> languages.<sup about="#mwt323" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-96" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-96&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-96" id="mwAo4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAo8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwApA">[</span>88<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwApE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwApI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuzzy_logic" title="Fuzzy logic" id="mwApM">Fuzzy logic</a> assigns a "degree of truth" between 0 and 1. It can therefore handle propositions that are vague and partially true.<sup about="#mwt326" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-97" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-97&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-97" id="mwApQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwApU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwApY">[</span>89<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwApc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwApg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-monotonic_logic" title="Non-monotonic logic" id="mwApk">Non-monotonic logics</a>, including logic programming with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negation_as_failure" title="Negation as failure" id="mwApo">negation as failure</a>, are designed to handle <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Default_reasoning" title="Default reasoning" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAps">default reasoning</a>.<sup about="#mwt327" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Default_reasoning_32-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Default reasoning&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Default_reasoning-32" id="mwApw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAp0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAp4">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAp8">]</span></span></a></sup> Other specialised versions of logic have been developed to describe many complex domains.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="15" id="mwAqA" aria-labelledby="Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Probabilistic_methods_for_uncertain_reasoning">Probabilistic methods for uncertain reasoning</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size skin-invert-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwAqE"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SimpleBayesNet.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwAqI"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SimpleBayesNet.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/SimpleBayesNet.svg/500px-SimpleBayesNet.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/SimpleBayesNet.svg/960px-SimpleBayesNet.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="575" data-file-height="325" data-file-type="drawing" height="198" width="350" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.4" id="mwAqM"></a><figcaption id="mwAqQ">A simple <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayesian_network" title="Bayesian network" id="mwAqU">Bayesian network</a>, with the associated <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conditional_probability_table" title="Conditional probability table" id="mwAqY">conditional probability tables</a></figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwAqc">Many problems in AI (including reasoning, planning, learning, perception, and robotics) require the agent to operate with incomplete or uncertain information. AI researchers have devised a number of tools to solve these problems using methods from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability" title="Probability" id="mwAqg">probability</a> theory and economics.<sup about="#mwt332" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Stoch_98-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Stoch&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Stoch-98&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Stoch-98" id="mwAqk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAqo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqs">[</span>90<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAqw">]</span></span></a></sup> Precise mathematical tools have been developed that analyse how an agent can make choices and plan, using <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_theory" title="Decision theory" id="mwAq0">decision theory</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_analysis" title="Decision analysis" id="mwAq4">decision analysis</a>,<sup about="#mwt335" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-99" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-99&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-99" id="mwAq8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwArA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArE">[</span>91<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArI">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_value_theory" title="Information value theory" class="mw-redirect" id="mwArM">information value theory</a>.<sup about="#mwt337" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-100" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-100&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-100" id="mwArQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwArU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArY">[</span>92<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArc">]</span></span></a></sup> These tools include models such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_decision_process" title="Markov decision process" id="mwArg">Markov decision processes</a>,<sup about="#mwt339" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-101" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-101&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-101" id="mwArk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAro"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArs">[</span>93<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwArw">]</span></span></a></sup> dynamic <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_network" title="Decision network" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAr0">decision networks</a>,<sup about="#mwt340" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Stochastic_temporal_models_102-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Stochastic temporal models&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Stochastic_temporal_models-102" id="mwAr4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAr8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAsA">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAsE">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory" title="Game theory" id="mwAsI">game theory</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanism_design" title="Mechanism design" id="mwAsM">mechanism design</a>.<sup about="#mwt342" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-103" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-103&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-103" id="mwAsQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAsU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAsY">[</span>95<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAsc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAsg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayesian_network" title="Bayesian network" id="mwAsk">Bayesian networks</a><sup about="#mwt359" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-104" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-104&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-104" id="mwAso"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAss"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAsw">[</span>96<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAs0">]</span></span></a></sup> are a tool that can be used for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_reasoning" title="Automated reasoning" id="mwAs4">reasoning</a> (using the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayesian_inference" title="Bayesian inference" id="mwAs8">Bayesian inference</a> algorithm),<sup about="#mwt343" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-106" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-106&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Compared with symbolic logic, formal Bayesian inference is computationally expensive. For inference to be tractable, most observations must be [[conditionally independent]] of one another. [[AdSense]] uses a Bayesian network with over 300&amp;nbsp;million edges to learn which ads to serve.{{Sfnp|Domingos|2015|loc=chpt. 6}}\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-106" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwAtA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAtE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAtI">[</span>i<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAtM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt364" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-107" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-107&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-107" id="mwAtQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAtU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAtY">[</span>98<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAtc">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mwAtg">learning</a> (using the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expectation–maximization_algorithm" title="Expectation–maximization algorithm" id="mwAtk">expectation–maximisation algorithm</a>),<sup about="#mwt349" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-109" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-109&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Expectation–maximisation, one of the most popular algorithms in machine learning, allows clustering in the presence of unknown [[latent variables]].{{Sfnp|Domingos|2015|p=210}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-109" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwAto"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAts"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAtw">[</span>j<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAt0">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt369" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-110" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-110&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-110" id="mwAt4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAt8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAuA">[</span>100<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAuE">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_planning_and_scheduling" title="Automated planning and scheduling" id="mwAuI">planning</a> (using <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_network" title="Decision network" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAuM">decision networks</a>)<sup about="#mwt371" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-111" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-111&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-111" id="mwAuQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAuU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAuY">[</span>101<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAuc">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_perception" title="Machine perception" id="mwAug">perception</a> (using <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_Bayesian_network" title="Dynamic Bayesian network" id="mwAuk">dynamic Bayesian networks</a>).<sup about="#mwt372" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Stochastic_temporal_models_102-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Stochastic temporal models&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Stochastic_temporal_models-102" id="mwAuo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAus"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAuw">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAu0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAu4">Probabilistic algorithms can also be used for filtering, prediction, smoothing, and finding explanations for streams of data, thus helping perception systems analyse processes that occur over time (e.g., <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidden_Markov_model" title="Hidden Markov model" id="mwAu8">hidden Markov models</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalman_filter" title="Kalman filter" id="mwAvA">Kalman filters</a>).<sup about="#mwt377" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Stochastic_temporal_models_102-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Stochastic temporal models&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Stochastic_temporal_models-102&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Stochastic_temporal_models-102" id="mwAvE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAvI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAvM">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAvQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwAvU"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EM_Clustering_of_Old_Faithful_data.gif" class="mw-file-description" id="mwAvY"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EM_Clustering_of_Old_Faithful_data.gif" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/EM_Clustering_of_Old_Faithful_data.gif/330px-EM_Clustering_of_Old_Faithful_data.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/69/EM_Clustering_of_Old_Faithful_data.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled 2x" data-file-width="360" data-file-height="309" data-file-type="bitmap" height="266" width="310" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.25" id="mwAvc"></a><figcaption id="mwAvg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expectation–maximization_algorithm" title="Expectation–maximization algorithm" id="mwAvk">Expectation–maximisation</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluster_analysis" title="Cluster analysis" id="mwAvo">clustering</a> of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Faithful" title="Old Faithful" id="mwAvs">Old Faithful</a> eruption data starts from a random guess but then successfully converges on an accurate clustering of the two physically distinct modes of eruption.</figcaption></figure>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="16" id="mwAvw" aria-labelledby="Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Classifiers_and_statistical_learning_methods">Classifiers and statistical learning methods</h3></div>
<p id="mwAv0">The simplest AI applications can be divided into two types: classifiers (e.g., "if shiny then diamond"), on one hand, and controllers (e.g., "if diamond then pick up"), on the other hand. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classifier_(mathematics)" title="Classifier (mathematics)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAv4">Classifiers</a><sup about="#mwt379" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-112" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-112&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-112" id="mwAv8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAwA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAwE">[</span>102<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAwI">]</span></span></a></sup> are functions that use <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattern_matching" title="Pattern matching" id="mwAwM">pattern matching</a> to determine the closest match. They can be fine-tuned based on chosen examples using <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supervised_learning" title="Supervised learning" id="mwAwQ">supervised learning</a>. Each pattern (also called an "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_variate" title="Random variate" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAwU">observation</a>") is labeled with a certain predefined class. All the observations combined with their class labels are known as a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_set" title="Data set" id="mwAwY">data set</a>. When a new observation is received, that observation is classified based on previous experience.<sup about="#mwt380" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Supervised_learning_54-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Supervised learning&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Supervised_learning-54" id="mwAwc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAwg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAwk">[</span>47<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAwo">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAws">There are many kinds of classifiers in use.<sup about="#mwt383" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-113" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-113&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-113" id="mwAww"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAw0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAw4">[</span>103<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAw8">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_tree" title="Decision tree" id="mwAxA">decision tree</a> is the simplest and most widely used symbolic machine learning algorithm.<sup about="#mwt386" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-114" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-114&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-114" id="mwAxE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAxI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAxM">[</span>104<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAxQ">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-nearest_neighbor" title="K-nearest neighbor" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAxU">K-nearest neighbour</a> algorithm was the most widely used analogical AI until the mid-1990s, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_methods" title="Kernel methods" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAxY">Kernel methods</a> such as the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support_vector_machine" title="Support vector machine" id="mwAxc">support vector machine</a> (SVM) displaced k-nearest neighbour in the 1990s.<sup about="#mwt390" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-115" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-115&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-115" id="mwAxg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAxk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAxo">[</span>105<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAxs">]</span></span></a></sup>
The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naive_Bayes_classifier" title="Naive Bayes classifier" id="mwAxw">naive Bayes classifier</a> is reportedly the "most widely used learner"<sup about="#mwt391" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEDomingos2015152_116-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEDomingos2015152&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEDomingos2015152-116&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Domingos&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2015&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;152&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDomingos2015152-116" id="mwAx0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAx4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAx8">[</span>106<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAyA">]</span></span></a></sup> at Google, due in part to its scalability.<sup about="#mwt396" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-117" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-117&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-117" id="mwAyE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAyI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAyM">[</span>107<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAyQ">]</span></span></a></sup>
<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_network" title="Artificial neural network" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAyU">Neural networks</a> are also used as classifiers.<sup about="#mwt397" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Neural_networks_118-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Neural networks&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Neural_networks-118" id="mwAyY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAyc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAyg">[</span>108<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAyk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="17" id="mwAyo" aria-labelledby="Artificial_neural_networks"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Artificial_neural_networks">Artificial neural networks</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwAys"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Artificial_neural_network.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwAyw"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Artificial_neural_network.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Artificial_neural_network.svg/250px-Artificial_neural_network.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Artificial_neural_network.svg/500px-Artificial_neural_network.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="560" data-file-height="500" data-file-type="drawing" height="223" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwAy0"></a><figcaption id="mwAy4">A neural network is an interconnected group of nodes, akin to the vast network of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron" title="Neuron" id="mwAy8">neurons</a> in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain" title="Human brain" id="mwAzA">human brain</a>.</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwAzE">An artificial neural network is based on a collection of nodes also known as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neurons" title="Artificial neurons" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAzI">artificial neurons</a>, which loosely model the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurons" title="Neurons" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAzM">neurons</a> in a biological brain. It is trained to recognise patterns; once trained, it can recognise those patterns in fresh data. There is an input, at least one hidden layer of nodes and an output. Each node applies a function and once the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighting" title="Weighting" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAzQ">weight</a> crosses its specified threshold, the data is transmitted to the next layer. A network is typically called a deep neural network if it has at least 2 hidden layers.<sup about="#mwt400" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Neural_networks_118-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Neural networks&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Neural_networks-118&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Neural_networks-118" id="mwAzU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAzY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAzc">[</span>108<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAzg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwAzk">Learning algorithms for neural networks use <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_search_(optimization)" title="Local search (optimization)" id="mwAzo">local search</a> to choose the weights that will get the right output for each input during training. The most common training technique is the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backpropagation" title="Backpropagation" id="mwAzs">backpropagation</a> algorithm.<sup about="#mwt404" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-119" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-119&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-119" id="mwAzw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAz0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAz4">[</span>109<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAz8">]</span></span></a></sup> Neural networks learn to model complex relationships between inputs and outputs and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattern_recognition" title="Pattern recognition" id="mwA0A">find patterns</a> in data. In theory, a neural network can learn any function.<sup about="#mwt408" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-120" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-120&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-120" id="mwA0E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA0I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA0M">[</span>110<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA0Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwA0U">In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feedforward_neural_network" title="Feedforward neural network" id="mwA0Y">feedforward neural networks</a> the signal passes in only one direction.<sup about="#mwt410" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-121" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-121&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-121" id="mwA0c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA0g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA0k">[</span>111<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA0o">]</span></span></a></sup> The term <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptron" title="Perceptron" id="mwA0s">perceptron</a> typically refers to a single-layer neural network.<sup about="#mwt412" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-122" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-122&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-122" id="mwA0w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA00"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA04">[</span>112<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA08">]</span></span></a></sup> In contrast, deep learning uses many layers.<sup about="#mwt417" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Deep_learning_123-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Deep learning&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Deep_learning-123&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Deep_learning-123" id="mwA1A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA1E"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA1I">[</span>113<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA1M">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recurrent_neural_network" title="Recurrent neural network" id="mwA1Q">Recurrent neural networks</a> (RNNs) feed the output signal back into the input, which allows short-term memories of previous input events. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_short-term_memory" title="Long short-term memory" id="mwA1U">Long short-term memory</a> networks (LSTMs) are recurrent neural networks that better preserve longterm dependencies and are less sensitive to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanishing_gradient_problem" title="Vanishing gradient problem" id="mwA1Y">vanishing gradient problem</a>.<sup about="#mwt419" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-124" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-124&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-124" id="mwA1c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA1g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA1k">[</span>114<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA1o">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolutional_neural_network" title="Convolutional neural network" id="mwA1s">Convolutional neural networks</a> (CNNs) use layers of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_(image_processing)" title="Kernel (image processing)" id="mwA1w">kernels</a> to more efficiently process local patterns. This local processing is especially important in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_processing" title="Image processing" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA10">image processing</a>, where the early CNN layers typically identify simple local patterns such as edges and curves, with subsequent layers detecting more complex patterns like textures, and eventually whole objects.<sup about="#mwt421" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-125" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-125&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-125" id="mwA14"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA18"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA2A">[</span>115<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA2E">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="18" id="mwA2I" aria-labelledby="Deep_learning"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Deep_learning">Deep learning</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwA2M"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AI-ML-DL.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwA2Q"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AI-ML-DL.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/AI-ML-DL.svg/250px-AI-ML-DL.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/AI-ML-DL.svg/500px-AI-ML-DL.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="748" data-file-height="826" data-file-type="drawing" height="232" width="210" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 0.85" id="mwA2U"></a><figcaption id="mwA2Y"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning" title="Deep learning" id="mwA2c">Deep learning</a> is a subset of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mwA2g">machine learning</a>, which is itself a subset of artificial intelligence.<sup about="#mwt424" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-journalimcms.org_126-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;journalimcms.org&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-journalimcms.org-126&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-journalimcms.org-126" id="mwA2k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA2o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA2s">[</span>116<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA2w">]</span></span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwA20"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning" title="Deep learning" id="mwA24">Deep learning</a> uses several layers of neurons between the network's inputs and outputs.<sup about="#mwt428" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Deep_learning_123-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Deep learning&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Deep_learning-123" id="mwA28"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA3A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA3E">[</span>113<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA3I">]</span></span></a></sup> The multiple layers can progressively extract higher-level features from the raw input. For example, in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_processing" title="Image processing" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA3M">image processing</a>, lower layers may identify edges, while higher layers may identify the concepts relevant to a human such as digits, letters, or faces.<sup about="#mwt425" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEDengYu2014199–200_127-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEDengYu2014199–200&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEDengYu2014199–200-127&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Deng&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Yu&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2014&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;199–200&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDengYu2014199–200-127" id="mwA3Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA3U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA3Y">[</span>117<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA3c">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwA3g">Deep learning has profoundly improved the performance of programs in many important subfields of artificial intelligence, including <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_vision" title="Computer vision" id="mwA3k">computer vision</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_recognition" title="Speech recognition" id="mwA3o">speech recognition</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing" title="Natural language processing" id="mwA3s">natural language processing</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_classification" title="Image classification" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA3w">image classification</a>,<sup about="#mwt429" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECiresanMeierSchmidhuber2012_128-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECiresanMeierSchmidhuber2012&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECiresanMeierSchmidhuber2012-128&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Ciresan&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Meier&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Schmidhuber&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2012&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECiresanMeierSchmidhuber2012-128" id="mwA30"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA34"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA38">[</span>118<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4A">]</span></span></a></sup> and others. The reason that deep learning performs so well in so many applications is not known as of 2021.<sup about="#mwt432" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021750_129-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021750&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021750-129&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;750&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021750-129" id="mwA4E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA4I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4M">[</span>119<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4Q">]</span></span></a></sup> The sudden success of deep learning in 2012–2015 did not occur because of some new discovery or theoretical breakthrough (deep neural networks and backpropagation had been described by many people, as far back as the 1950s)<sup about="#mwt435" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-136" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-136&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Some form of deep neural networks (without a specific learning algorithm) were described by:\n[[Warren S. McCulloch]] and [[Walter Pitts]] (1943);{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=17}}\n[[Alan Turing]] (1948);{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=785}}\n[[Karl Steinbuch]] and [[Roger David Joseph]] (1961).{{Sfnp|Schmidhuber|2022|loc=sect. 5}}\nDeep or recurrent networks that learned (or used gradient descent) were developed by:\n[[Frank Rosenblatt]] (1957);{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=785}}\n[[Oliver Selfridge]] (1959);{{Sfnp|Schmidhuber|2022|loc=sect. 5}}\n[[Alexey Ivakhnenko]] and [[Valentin Lapa]] (1965);{{Sfnp|Schmidhuber|2022|loc=sect. 6}}\n[[Kaoru Nakano]] (1971);{{Sfnp|Schmidhuber|2022|loc=sect. 7}}\n[[Shun-Ichi Amari]] (1972); {{Sfnp|Schmidhuber|2022|loc=sect. 7}} and [[John Joseph Hopfield]] (1982).{{Sfnp|Schmidhuber|2022|loc=sect. 7}}\nPrecursors to backpropagation were developed by:\n[[Henry J. Kelley]] (1960);{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=785}}\n[[Arthur E. Bryson]] (1962);{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=785}}\n[[Stuart Dreyfus]] (1962);{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=785}}\n[[Arthur E. Bryson]] and [[Yu-Chi Ho]] (1969).{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=785}}\nBackpropagation was independently developed by:\n[[Seppo Linnainmaa]] (1970);{{Sfnp|Schmidhuber|2022|loc=sect. 8}} and [[Paul Werbos]] (1974).{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=785}}\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-136" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwA4U"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA4Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4c">[</span>k<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA4g">]</span></span></a></sup> but because of two factors: the increase in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compute_(machine_learning)" title="Compute (machine learning)" id="mwA4k">computer power</a> (including the hundred-fold increase in speed by switching to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPU" title="GPU" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA4o">GPUs</a>) and the availability of vast amounts of training data, especially the giant <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_datasets_for_machine-learning_research" title="List of datasets for machine-learning research" id="mwA4s">curated datasets</a> used for benchmark testing, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ImageNet" title="ImageNet" id="mwA4w">ImageNet</a>.<sup about="#mwt483" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-138" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-138&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Geoffrey Hinton]] said, of his work on neural networks in the 1990s, \&quot;our labeled datasets were thousands of times too small. [And] our computers were millions of times too slow.\&quot;&lt;ref&gt;Quoted in {{Harvtxt|Christian|2020|p=22}}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-138" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwA40"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA44"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA48">[</span>l<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA5A">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="19" id="mwA5E" aria-labelledby="GPT"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="GPT">GPT</h3></div>
<p id="mwA5I"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer" title="Generative pre-trained transformer" id="mwA5M">Generative pre-trained transformers</a> (GPTs) are <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model" title="Large language model" id="mwA5Q">large language models</a> (LLMs) that generate text based on the semantic relationships between words in sentences. Text-based GPT models are pre-trained on a large <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_of_text" title="Corpus of text" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA5U">corpus of text</a> that can be from the Internet. The pretraining consists of predicting the next <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexical_analysis" title="Lexical analysis" id="mwA5Y">token</a> (a token being usually a word, subword, or punctuation). Throughout this pretraining, GPT models accumulate knowledge about the world and can then generate human-like text by repeatedly predicting the next token. Typically, a subsequent training phase makes the model more truthful, useful, and harmless, usually with a technique called <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinforcement_learning_from_human_feedback" title="Reinforcement learning from human feedback" id="mwA5c">reinforcement learning from human feedback</a> (RLHF). Current GPT models are prone to generating falsehoods called "hallucinations". These can be reduced with RLHF and quality data, but the problem has been getting worse for reasoning systems.<sup about="#mwt495" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-139" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-139&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-139" id="mwA5g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA5k"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA5o">[</span>127<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA5s">]</span></span></a></sup> Such systems are used in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbot" title="Chatbot" id="mwA5w">chatbots</a>, which allow people to ask a question or request a task in simple text.<sup about="#mwt490" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESmith2023_140-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESmith2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2023-140&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Smith&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2023-140" id="mwA50"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA54"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA58">[</span>128<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA6A">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt498" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-141" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-141&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-141" id="mwA6E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA6I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA6M">[</span>129<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA6Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwA6U">Current models and services include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT" title="ChatGPT" id="mwA6Y">ChatGPT</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_AI" title="Claude AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA6c">Claude</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Gemini" title="Google Gemini" id="mwA6g">Gemini</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Copilot" title="Microsoft Copilot" id="mwA6k">Copilot</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_AI" title="Meta AI" id="mwA6o">Meta AI</a>.<sup about="#mwt504" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-142" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-142&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-142" id="mwA6s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA6w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA60">[</span>130<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA64">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimodal_learning" title="Multimodal learning" id="mwA68">Multimodal</a> GPT models can process different types of data (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modality_(human–computer_interaction)" title="Modality (human–computer interaction)" id="mwA7A">modalities</a>) such as images, videos, sound, and text.<sup about="#mwt499" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarmouyet2023_143-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMarmouyet2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarmouyet2023-143&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Marmouyet&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarmouyet2023-143" id="mwA7E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA7I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA7M">[</span>131<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA7Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="20" id="mwA7U" aria-labelledby="Hardware_and_software"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Hardware_and_software">Hardware and software</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt505" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwA7Y" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Programming languages for artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hardware for artificial intelligence&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt506" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt505" id="mwA7c">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_languages_for_artificial_intelligence" title="Programming languages for artificial intelligence" class="mw-redirect">Programming languages for artificial intelligence</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardware_for_artificial_intelligence" title="Hardware for artificial intelligence">Hardware for artificial intelligence</a></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwA7g"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raspberry_Pi_AI_Kit_for_Raspberry_Pi_5_complete_Kit_07.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwA7k"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raspberry_Pi_AI_Kit_for_Raspberry_Pi_5_complete_Kit_07.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Raspberry_Pi_AI_Kit_for_Raspberry_Pi_5_complete_Kit_07.jpg/250px-Raspberry_Pi_AI_Kit_for_Raspberry_Pi_5_complete_Kit_07.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Raspberry_Pi_AI_Kit_for_Raspberry_Pi_5_complete_Kit_07.jpg/500px-Raspberry_Pi_AI_Kit_for_Raspberry_Pi_5_complete_Kit_07.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="4831" data-file-height="3221" data-file-type="bitmap" height="167" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwA7o"></a><figcaption id="mwA7s">Raspberry Pi AI Kit</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwA7w">In the late 2010s, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit" title="Graphics processing unit" id="mwA70">graphics processing units</a> (GPUs) that were increasingly designed with AI-specific enhancements and used with specialised <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TensorFlow" title="TensorFlow" id="mwA74">TensorFlow</a> software had replaced previously used <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_processing_unit" title="Central processing unit" id="mwA78">central processing unit</a> (CPUs) as the dominant means for large-scale (commercial and academic) <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mwA8A">machine learning</a> models' training.<sup about="#mwt507" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKobielus2019_144-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEKobielus2019&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEKobielus2019-144&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Kobielus&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2019&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKobielus2019-144" id="mwA8E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA8I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA8M">[</span>132<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA8Q">]</span></span></a></sup> Specialised <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language" title="Programming language" id="mwA8U">programming languages</a> such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prolog" title="Prolog" id="mwA8Y">Prolog</a> were used in early AI research,<sup about="#mwt512" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-145" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-145&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-145" id="mwA8c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA8g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA8k">[</span>133<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA8o">]</span></span></a></sup> but <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General-purpose_programming_language" title="General-purpose programming language" id="mwA8s">general-purpose programming languages</a> like <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language)" title="Python (programming language)" id="mwA8w">Python</a> have become predominant.<sup about="#mwt515" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-146" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-146&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-146" id="mwA80"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA84"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA88">[</span>134<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA9A">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwA9E">The transistor density in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_circuit" title="Integrated circuit" id="mwA9I">integrated circuits</a> has been observed to roughly double every 18 months—a trend known as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moore's_law" title="Moore's law" id="mwA9M">Moore's law</a>, named after the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intel" title="Intel" id="mwA9Q">Intel</a> co-founder <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Moore" title="Gordon Moore" id="mwA9U">Gordon Moore</a>, who first identified it. Improvements in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPUs" title="GPUs" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA9Y">GPUs</a> have been even faster,<sup about="#mwt518" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-147" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-147&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-147" id="mwA9c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA9g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA9k">[</span>135<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA9o">]</span></span></a></sup> a trend sometimes called <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huang's_law" title="Huang's law" id="mwA9s">Huang's law</a>,<sup about="#mwt521" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-148" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-148&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-148" id="mwA9w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwA90"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA94">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwA98">]</span></span></a></sup> named after <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia" title="Nvidia" id="mwA-A">Nvidia</a> co-founder and CEO <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jensen_Huang" title="Jensen Huang" id="mwA-E">Jensen Huang</a>.</p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="21" id="mwA-I" aria-labelledby="Applications"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Applications">Applications</h2></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt522" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwA-M" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Applications of artificial intelligence&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt523" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt522" id="mwA-Q">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applications_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Applications of artificial intelligence">Applications of artificial intelligence</a></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwA-U"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AI_Overviews_result_for_What_is_Wikipedia,_2_March_2026.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwA-Y"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AI_Overviews_result_for_What_is_Wikipedia,_2_March_2026.png" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/AI_Overviews_result_for_What_is_Wikipedia%2C_2_March_2026.png/250px-AI_Overviews_result_for_What_is_Wikipedia%2C_2_March_2026.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/AI_Overviews_result_for_What_is_Wikipedia%2C_2_March_2026.png/500px-AI_Overviews_result_for_What_is_Wikipedia%2C_2_March_2026.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="1336" data-file-height="1356" data-file-type="bitmap" height="254" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwA-c"></a><figcaption id="mwA-g"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_Overviews" title="AI Overviews" id="mwA-k">AI Overviews</a>, an example of AI use on search engines</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwA-o">AI and machine learning technology is used in most of the essential applications of the 2020s, including:</p>
<ul id="mwA-s"><li id="mwA-w"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engines" title="Search engines" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA-0">search engines</a> (such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Search" title="Google Search" id="mwA-4">Google Search</a>)</li>
<li id="mwA-8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Targeted_advertising" title="Targeted advertising" id="mwA_A">targeting online advertisements</a></li>
<li id="mwA_E"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recommendation_systems" title="Recommendation systems" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA_I">recommendation systems</a> (offered by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix" title="Netflix" id="mwA_M">Netflix</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube" title="YouTube" id="mwA_Q">YouTube</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company)" title="Amazon (company)" id="mwA_U">Amazon</a>) driving <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_traffic" title="Internet traffic" id="mwA_Y">internet traffic</a></li>
<li id="mwA_c"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketing_and_artificial_intelligence" title="Marketing and artificial intelligence" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA_g">targeted advertising</a> (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AdSense" title="AdSense" class="mw-redirect" id="mwA_k">AdSense</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook" title="Facebook" id="mwA_o">Facebook</a>)</li>
<li id="mwA_s"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_assistant" title="Virtual assistant" id="mwA_w">virtual assistants</a> (such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siri" title="Siri" id="mwA_0">Siri</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Alexa" title="Amazon Alexa" id="mwA_4">Alexa</a>)</li>
<li id="mwA_8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_vehicles" title="Autonomous vehicles" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBAA">autonomous vehicles</a> (including <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle" title="Unmanned aerial vehicle" id="mwBAE">drones</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_driver-assistance_system" title="Advanced driver-assistance system" id="mwBAI">ADAS</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-driving_cars" title="Self-driving cars" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBAM">self-driving cars</a>)</li>
<li id="mwBAQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_language_translation" title="Automatic language translation" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBAU">automatic language translation</a> (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Translator" title="Microsoft Translator" id="mwBAY">Microsoft Translator</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Translate" title="Google Translate" id="mwBAc">Google Translate</a>)</li>
<li id="mwBAg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_recognition_system" title="Facial recognition system" id="mwBAk">facial recognition</a> (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Computer" title="Apple Computer" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBAo">Apple</a>'s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FaceID" title="FaceID" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBAs">FaceID</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms" title="Meta Platforms" id="mwBAw">Facebook</a>'s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepFace" title="DeepFace" id="mwBA0">DeepFace</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google" title="Google" id="mwBA4">Google</a>'s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FaceNet" title="FaceNet" id="mwBA8">FaceNet</a>)</li>
<li id="mwBBA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_labeling" title="Image labeling" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBBE">image labelling</a> (used by Facebook, Apple's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photos_(Apple)" title="Photos (Apple)" id="mwBBI">Photos</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok" title="TikTok" id="mwBBM">TikTok</a>).</li></ul>

<p id="mwBBQ">The deployment of AI may be overseen by a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_automation_officer" title="Chief automation officer" id="mwBBU">chief automation officer</a> (CAO).</p>

<section data-mw-section-id="22" id="mwBBY" aria-labelledby="AI-assisted_software_development"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="AI-assisted_software_development">AI-assisted software development</h3></div>
