<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt846" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBkY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Environmental impacts of artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;AI build-out financing&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt847" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt846" id="mwBkc">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_impacts_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Environmental impacts of artificial intelligence" class="mw-redirect">Environmental impacts of artificial intelligence</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_build-out_financing" title="AI build-out financing">AI build-out financing</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwBkg"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2015-_Data_center_power_demand_-_US.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwBkk"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2015-_Data_center_power_demand_-_US.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/2015-_Data_center_power_demand_-_US.svg/330px-2015-_Data_center_power_demand_-_US.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/2015-_Data_center_power_demand_-_US.svg/960px-2015-_Data_center_power_demand_-_US.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="675" data-file-type="drawing" height="174" width="310" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.25" id="mwBko"></a><figcaption id="mwBks">Fuelled by a growth in AI, data centres' demand for power increased in the 2020s.<sup about="#mwt850" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-WashPost_20251225_237-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;WashPost_20251225&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-WashPost_20251225-237&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-WashPost_20251225-237" id="mwBkw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBk0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBk4">[</span>225<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBk8">]</span></span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwBlA">Technology companies have built electricity and artificial intelligence infrastructure to facilitate the AI boom of the 2020s. A 2025 report from the consulting firm <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKinsey_&amp;_Company" title="McKinsey &amp; Company" id="mwBlE">McKinsey &amp; Company</a> estimated that by 2030, $2.7 trillion would be invested into AI infrastructure and data centres in the US, surpassing World War II's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Project" title="Manhattan Project" id="mwBlI">Manhattan Project</a> every month.<sup about="#mwt853" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-238" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-238&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-238" id="mwBlM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBlQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlU">[</span>226<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBlc">In January 2024, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Energy_Agency" title="International Energy Agency" id="mwBlg">International Energy Agency</a> (IEA) released <i id="mwBlk">Electricity 2024, Analysis and Forecast to 2026</i>.<sup about="#mwt856" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-239" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-239&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-239" id="mwBlo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBls"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBlw">[</span>227<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBl0">]</span></span></a></sup> This is the first IEA report to make projections for data centres and power consumption by AI and cryptocurrency. The report states that power demand for these uses might double by 2026, with the additional power consumption equaling that of Japan.<sup about="#mwt859" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-240" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-240&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-240" id="mwBl4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBl8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmA">[</span>228<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBmI">Power consumption by AI is responsible for an increase in fossil fuel use, and has delayed closings of obsolete, carbon-emitting coal energy facilities. A ChatGPT search involves 10 times as much electrical energy as a Google search.<sup about="#mwt862" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-241" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-241&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-241" id="mwBmM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBmQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmU">[</span>229<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBmc">A 2024 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldman_Sachs" title="Goldman Sachs" id="mwBmg">Goldman Sachs</a> research paper, <i id="mwBmk">AI Data Centers and the Coming US Power Demand Surge</i>, found "US power demand (is) likely to experience growth not seen in a generation...." and forecasts that, by 2030, US data centres will consume 8% of US power, as opposed to 3% in 2022, presaging growth for the electrical power generation industry by a variety of means.<sup about="#mwt865" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-242" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-242&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-242" id="mwBmo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBms"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBmw">[</span>230<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBm0">]</span></span></a></sup> Data centres' need for more and more electrical power is such that they might max out the electrical grid. The Big Tech companies counter that AI can be used to maximise the utilisation of the grid by all.<sup about="#mwt868" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-243" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-243&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-243" id="mwBm4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBm8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnA">[</span>231<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBnI">In 2024, <i id="mwBnM">The Wall Street Journal</i> reported that big AI companies have begun negotiations with the US nuclear power providers to provide electricity to the data centres. In March 2024, Amazon purchased a Pennsylvania nuclear-powered data centre for US$650 million.<sup about="#mwt871" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-244" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-244&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-244" id="mwBnQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBnU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnY">[</span>232<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBnc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBng">In September 2024, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft" title="Microsoft" id="mwBnk">Microsoft</a> announced an agreement with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constellation_Energy" title="Constellation Energy" id="mwBno">Constellation Energy</a> to re-open the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Mile_Island" title="Three Mile Island" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBns">Three Mile Island</a> nuclear power plant to provide Microsoft with 100% of all electric power produced by the plant for 20 years. Reopening the plant, which suffered a partial nuclear meltdown of its Unit 2 reactor in 1979, will require Constellation to get through strict regulatory processes which will include extensive safety scrutiny from the US <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_Regulatory_Commission" title="Nuclear Regulatory Commission" id="mwBnw">Nuclear Regulatory Commission</a>. If approved (this will be the first ever US re-commissioning of a nuclear plant), over 835 megawatts of power – enough for 800,000 homes – will be produced. The cost for re-opening and upgrading is estimated at US$1.6 billion and is dependent on tax breaks for nuclear power contained in the 2022 US <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflation_Reduction_Act" title="Inflation Reduction Act" id="mwBn0">Inflation Reduction Act</a>.<sup about="#mwt874" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-245" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-245&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-245" id="mwBn4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBn8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoA">[</span>233<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoE">]</span></span></a></sup> As of 2024, the US government and the state of Michigan have been investing almost US$2 billion to reopen the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palisades_Nuclear_Generating_Station" title="Palisades Nuclear Generating Station" id="mwBoI">Palisades nuclear reactor</a> on Lake Michigan. Closed since 2022, the plant was scheduled to be reopened in October 2025.<sup about="#mwt877" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-246" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-246&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-246" id="mwBoM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBoQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoU">[</span>234<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBoY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBoc">After the last approval in September 2023, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan" title="Taiwan" id="mwBog">Taiwan</a> suspended the approval of data centres north of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taoyuan,_Taiwan" title="Taoyuan, Taiwan" id="mwBok">Taoyuan</a> with a capacity of more than 5 MW in 2024, due to power supply shortages.<sup about="#mwt880" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DatacenterDynamics_247-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;DatacenterDynamics&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-DatacenterDynamics-247&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-DatacenterDynamics-247" id="mwBoo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBos"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBow">[</span>235<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBo0">]</span></span></a></sup> Taiwan aims to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_power_phase-out" title="Nuclear power phase-out" id="mwBo4">phase out nuclear power</a> by 2025.<sup about="#mwt881" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DatacenterDynamics_247-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;DatacenterDynamics&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-DatacenterDynamics-247" id="mwBo8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBpA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpE">[</span>235<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpI">]</span></span></a></sup></p> 

<p id="mwBpM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore" title="Singapore" id="mwBpQ">Singapore</a> imposed a ban on the opening of data centres in 2019 due to electric power, but lifted it in 2022.<sup about="#mwt882" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-DatacenterDynamics_247-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;DatacenterDynamics&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-DatacenterDynamics-247" id="mwBpU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBpY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpc">[</span>235<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBpg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBpk">Although most nuclear plants in Japan have been shut down after the 2011 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fukushima_nuclear_accident" title="Fukushima nuclear accident" id="mwBpo">Fukushima nuclear accident</a>, according to an October 2024 <i id="mwBps">Bloomberg</i> article in Japanese, cloud gaming services company Ubitus, in which Nvidia has a stake, is looking for land in Japan near a nuclear power plant for a new data centre for generative AI.<sup about="#mwt885" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-bloombergjp_248-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;bloombergjp&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-bloombergjp-248&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-bloombergjp-248" id="mwBpw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBp0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBp4">[</span>236<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBp8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBqA">On 1 November 2024, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Energy_Regulatory_Commission" title="Federal Energy Regulatory Commission" id="mwBqE">Federal Energy Regulatory Commission</a> (FERC) rejected an application submitted by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talen_Energy" title="Talen Energy" id="mwBqI">Talen Energy</a> for approval to supply some electricity from the nuclear power station <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_Steam_Electric_Station" title="Susquehanna Steam Electric Station" id="mwBqM">Susquehanna</a> to Amazon's data centre.<sup about="#mwt888" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Bloomberg20241104_249-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Bloomberg20241104&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Bloomberg20241104-249&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Bloomberg20241104-249" id="mwBqQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqY">[</span>237<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqc">]</span></span></a></sup>
According to the Commission Chairman <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_L._Phillips" title="Willie L. Phillips" id="mwBqg">Willie L. Phillips</a>, it is a burden on the electricity grid as well as a significant cost-shifting concern to households and other business sectors.<sup about="#mwt889" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Bloomberg20241104_249-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Bloomberg20241104&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Bloomberg20241104-249" id="mwBqk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBqo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqs">[</span>237<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBqw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBq0">In 2025, a report prepared by the IEA estimated the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions" title="Greenhouse gas emissions" id="mwBq4">greenhouse gas emissions</a> from the energy consumption of AI at 180 million tons. By 2035, these emissions could rise to 300–500 million tonnes depending on what measures will be taken. This is below 1.5% of the energy sector emissions. The emissions reduction potential of AI was estimated at 5% of the energy sector emissions, but <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebound_effect_(conservation)" title="Rebound effect (conservation)" id="mwBq8">rebound effects</a> (for example if people switch from public transport to autonomous cars) can reduce it.<sup about="#mwt892" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-250" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-250&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-250" id="mwBrA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBrE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrI">[</span>238<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBrM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBrQ">In June 2026, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_University_Institute_for_Water,_Environment_and_Health" title="United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health" id="mwBrU">United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health</a> released a report about cumulative environmental impacts of AI, not only carbon. The report found that AI has significant negative impacts on land, water, and climate, as it uses large amounts of electricity, requires <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mining" title="Mining" id="mwBrY">mining</a> of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_raw_materials" title="Critical raw materials" id="mwBrc">minerals</a>, and generates large amounts of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_waste" title="Electronic waste" id="mwBrg">electronic waste</a>. In 2025, data centres consumed more electricity than Saudi Arabia, and ChatGPT alone consumed an amount of water equivalent to the needs of 500,000 people in Sub-Saharan Africa. The negative impacts are not distributed equally across the planet but are concentrated in some places. Data centres are often built in places already suffering from water deficit. For example, AI deployment has already led to an increase in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_scarcity" title="Water scarcity" id="mwBrk">water scarcity</a> in Mexico and Uruguay. It created problems with energy supply in Ireland, which forbade construction of new data centres near Dublin until 2028. Measures can involve tradeoffs, for example, transitioning from coal to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioenergy" title="Bioenergy" id="mwBro">bioenergy</a> reduces carbon footprint but increases the impact on land and water. Energy efficiency might not reduce environmental impact, because as AI becomes more efficient, it also becomes cheaper and more widely used.<sup about="#mwt895" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-UN_13-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;UN&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-UN-13&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-UN-13" id="mwBrs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBrw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBr0">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBr4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="40" id="mwBr8" aria-labelledby="Misinformation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Misinformation">Misinformation</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt896" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBsA" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Content moderation&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt897" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt896" id="mwBsE">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_moderation" title="Content moderation">Content moderation</a></div>
<p id="mwBsI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube" title="YouTube" id="mwBsM">YouTube</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook" title="Facebook" id="mwBsQ">Facebook</a> and others use <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recommender_system" title="Recommender system" id="mwBsU">recommender systems</a> to guide users to more content. These AI programs were given the goal of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_optimization" title="Mathematical optimization" id="mwBsY">maximising</a> user engagement (that is, the only goal was to keep people watching). The AI learned that users tended to choose <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misinformation" title="Misinformation" id="mwBsc">misinformation</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy_theories" title="Conspiracy theories" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBsg">conspiracy theories</a>, and extreme <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_(politics)" title="Partisan (politics)" id="mwBsk">partisan</a> content, and, to keep them watching, the AI recommended more of it. Users also tended to watch more content on the same subject, so the AI led people into <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filter_bubbles" title="Filter bubbles" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBso">filter bubbles</a> where they received multiple versions of the same misinformation.<sup about="#mwt898" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENicas2018_251-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTENicas2018&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTENicas2018-251&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Nicas&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2018&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENicas2018-251" id="mwBss"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBsw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBs0">[</span>239<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBs4">]</span></span></a></sup> This convinced many users that the misinformation was true, and ultimately undermined trust in institutions, the media and the government.<sup about="#mwt903" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-252" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-252&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-252" id="mwBs8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtE">[</span>240<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtI">]</span></span></a></sup> The AI program had correctly learned to maximise its goal, but the result was harmful to society. After the U.S. election in 2016, major technology companies took some steps to mitigate the problem.<sup about="#mwt906" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-253" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-253&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-253" id="mwBtM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBtQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtU">[</span>241<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBtc">In the early 2020s, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI" title="Generative AI" id="mwBtg">generative AI</a> began to create images, audio, and texts that are virtually indistinguishable from real photographs, recordings, or human writing,<sup about="#mwt918" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-254" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-254&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-254" id="mwBtk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBto"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBts">[</span>242<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBtw">]</span></span></a></sup> while realistic AI-generated videos became feasible in the mid-2020s.<sup about="#mwt921" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-255" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-255&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-255" id="mwBt0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBt4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBt8">[</span>243<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt924" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-256" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-256&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-256" id="mwBuE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBuI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuM">[</span>244<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt927" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-257" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-257&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-257" id="mwBuU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBuY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuc">[</span>245<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBug">]</span></span></a></sup> It is possible for bad actors to use this technology to create massive amounts of misinformation and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_propaganda" title="Computational propaganda" id="mwBuk">computational propaganda</a> through techniques such as deepfakes.<sup about="#mwt907" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWilliams2023_258-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEWilliams2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilliams2023-258&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Williams&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilliams2023-258" id="mwBuo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBus"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBuw">[</span>246<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBu0">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt910" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESamoilenkoSuvorova2023_259-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESamoilenkoSuvorova2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESamoilenkoSuvorova2023-259&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Samoilenko&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Suvorova&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESamoilenkoSuvorova2023-259" id="mwBu4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBu8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvA">[</span>247<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvE">]</span></span></a></sup> AI pioneer and Nobel Prize-winning computer scientist <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton" title="Geoffrey Hinton" id="mwBvI">Geoffrey Hinton</a> expressed concern about AI enabling "authoritarian leaders to manipulate their electorates" on a large scale, among other risks.<sup about="#mwt913" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTETaylorHern2023_260-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTETaylorHern2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTETaylorHern2023-260&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Taylor&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hern&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaylorHern2023-260" id="mwBvM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBvQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvU">[</span>248<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvY">]</span></span></a></sup> The ability to influence electorates has been proved in at least one study. This same study shows more inaccurate statements from the models when they advocate for candidates of the political right.<sup about="#mwt930" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-261" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-261&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-261" id="mwBvc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBvg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvk">[</span>249<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBvo">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBvs">AI researchers at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft" title="Microsoft" id="mwBvw">Microsoft</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI" title="OpenAI" id="mwBv0">OpenAI</a>, universities and other organisations have suggested using "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_of_personhood#Approaches" title="Proof of personhood" id="mwBv4">personhood credentials</a>" as a way to overcome online deception enabled by AI models.<sup about="#mwt933" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-262" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-262&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-262" id="mwBv8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBwA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwE">[</span>250<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwI">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="41" id="mwBwM" aria-labelledby="Algorithmic_bias_and_fairness"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Algorithmic_bias_and_fairness">Algorithmic bias and fairness</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt934" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwBwQ" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Algorithmic bias&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Fairness (machine learning)&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt935" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt934" id="mwBwU">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithmic_bias" title="Algorithmic bias">Algorithmic bias</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairness_(machine_learning)" title="Fairness (machine learning)">Fairness (machine learning)</a></div>

<p id="mwBwY">Machine learning applications can be <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithmic_bias" title="Algorithmic bias" id="mwBwc">biased</a><sup about="#mwt936" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-264" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-264&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;In statistics, a [[Bias (statistics)|bias]] is a systematic error or deviation from the correct value. But in the context of [[Fairness (machine learning)|fairness]], it refers to a tendency in favour or against a certain group or individual characteristic, usually in a way that is considered unfair or harmful. A statistically unbiased AI system that produces disparate outcomes for different demographic groups may thus be viewed as biased in the ethical sense.&lt;ref name=\&quot;Samuel-2022\&quot;/&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-264" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwBwg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBwk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBwo">[</span>m<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBws">]</span></span></a></sup> if they learn from biased data.<sup about="#mwt942" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERose2023_265-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERose2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERose2023-265&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Rose&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERose2023-265" id="mwBww"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBw0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBw4">[</span>252<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBw8">]</span></span></a></sup> The developers may not be aware that the bias exists.<sup about="#mwt945" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECNA2019_266-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECNA2019&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECNA2019-266&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;CNA&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2019&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECNA2019-266" id="mwBxA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxI">[</span>253<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxM">]</span></span></a></sup> Discriminatory behaviour by some LLMs can be observed in their output.<sup about="#mwt956" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-267" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-267&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-267" id="mwBxQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxY">[</span>254<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxc">]</span></span></a></sup> Bias can be introduced by the way <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training_data" title="Training data" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBxg">training data</a> is selected and by the way a model is deployed.<sup about="#mwt948" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGoffrey200817_268-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEGoffrey200817&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoffrey200817-268&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Goffrey&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2008&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;17&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoffrey200817-268" id="mwBxk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBxo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxs">[</span>255<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBxw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt951" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERose2023_265-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERose2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERose2023-265&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Rose&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERose2023-265" id="mwBx0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBx4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBx8">[</span>252<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwByA">]</span></span></a></sup> If a biased algorithm is used to make decisions that can seriously <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harm" title="Harm" id="mwByE">harm</a> people (as it can in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_equity" title="Health equity" id="mwByI">medicine</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_rating" title="Credit rating" id="mwByM">finance</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recruitment" title="Recruitment" id="mwByQ">recruitment</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_housing" title="Public housing" id="mwByU">housing</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Policing" title="Policing" class="mw-redirect" id="mwByY">policing</a>) then the algorithm may cause <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination" title="Discrimination" id="mwByc">discrimination</a>.<sup about="#mwt961" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-269" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-269&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-269" id="mwByg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwByk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwByo">[</span>256<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBys">]</span></span></a></sup> The field of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairness_(machine_learning)" title="Fairness (machine learning)" id="mwByw">fairness</a> studies how to prevent harms from algorithmic biases.</p>

<p id="mwBy0">On 28 June 2015, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Photos" title="Google Photos" id="mwBy4">Google Photos</a>'s new image labelling feature mistakenly identified Jacky Alcine and a friend as "gorillas" because they were black. The system was trained on a dataset that contained very few images of black people,<sup about="#mwt962" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian202025_270-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian202025&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202025-270&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;25&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202025-270" id="mwBy8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBzA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzE">[</span>257<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzI">]</span></span></a></sup> a problem called "sample size disparity".<sup about="#mwt965" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995_271-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995-271&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;995&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995-271" id="mwBzM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBzQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzU">[</span>258<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzY">]</span></span></a></sup> Google "fixed" this problem by preventing the system from labelling <i id="mwBzc">anything</i> as a "gorilla". Eight years later, in 2023, Google Photos still could not identify a gorilla, and neither could similar products from Apple, Facebook, Microsoft and Amazon.<sup about="#mwt968" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGrantHill2023_272-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEGrantHill2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrantHill2023-272&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Grant&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hill&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrantHill2023-272" id="mwBzg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBzk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzo">[</span>259<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBzs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwBzw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COMPAS_(software)" title="COMPAS (software)" id="mwBz0">COMPAS</a> is a commercial program widely used by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._court" title="U.S. court" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBz4">U.S. courts</a> to assess the likelihood of a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defendant" title="Defendant" id="mwBz8">defendant</a> becoming a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recidivist" title="Recidivist" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB0A">recidivist</a>. In 2016, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Angwin" title="Julia Angwin" id="mwB0E">Julia Angwin</a> at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ProPublica" title="ProPublica" id="mwB0I">ProPublica</a> discovered that COMPAS exhibited racial bias, despite the fact that the program was not told the races of the defendants. Although the error rate for both whites and blacks was calibrated equal at exactly 61%, the errors for each race were different—the system consistently overestimated the chance that a black person would re-offend and would underestimate the chance that a white person would not re-offend.<sup about="#mwt971" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELarsonAngwin2016_273-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELarsonAngwin2016&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELarsonAngwin2016-273&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Larson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Angwin&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2016&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELarsonAngwin2016-273" id="mwB0M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB0Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0U">[</span>260<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0Y">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2017, several researchers<sup about="#mwt974" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-275" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-275&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Including [[Jon Kleinberg]] ([[Cornell University]]), Sendhil Mullainathan ([[University of Chicago]]), Cynthia Chouldechova ([[Carnegie Mellon]]) and Sam Corbett-Davis ([[Stanford]]){{Sfnp|Christian|2020|p=67–70}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-275" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwB0c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB0g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0k">[</span>n<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB0o">]</span></span></a></sup> showed that it was mathematically impossible for COMPAS to accommodate all possible measures of fairness when the base rates of re-offence were different for whites and blacks in the data.<sup about="#mwt982" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-276" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-276&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-276" id="mwB0s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB0w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB00">[</span>262<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB04">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB08">A program can make biased decisions even if the data does not explicitly mention a problematic feature (such as "race" or "gender"). The feature will correlate with other features (like "address", "shopping history" or "first name"), and the program will make the same decisions based on these features as it would on "race" or "gender".<sup about="#mwt987" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-277" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-277&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-277" id="mwB1A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB1E"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1I">[</span>263<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1M">]</span></span></a></sup> Moritz Hardt said "the most robust fact in this research area is that fairness through blindness doesn't work."<sup about="#mwt989" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-278" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-278&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-278" id="mwB1Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB1U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1Y">[</span>264<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1c">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB1g">Criticism of COMPAS highlighted that machine learning models are designed to make "predictions" that are only valid if we assume that the future will resemble the past. If they are trained on data that includes the results of racist decisions in the past, machine learning models must predict that racist decisions will be made in the future. If an application then uses these predictions as <i id="mwB1k">recommendations</i>, some of these "recommendations" will likely be racist.<sup about="#mwt999" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-279" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-279&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-279" id="mwB1o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB1s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB1w">[</span>265<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB10">]</span></span></a></sup> Thus, machine learning is not well suited to help make decisions in areas where there is hope that the future will be <i id="mwB14">better</i> than the past. It is descriptive rather than prescriptive.<sup about="#mwt990" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-281" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-281&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Moritz Hardt (a director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems]]) argues that machine learning \&quot;is fundamentally the wrong tool for a lot of domains, where you're trying to design interventions and mechanisms that change the world.\&quot;&lt;ref&gt;Quoted in {{Harvtxt|Christian|2020|p=80}}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-281" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwB18"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB2A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2E">[</span>o<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2I">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB2M">Bias and unfairness may go undetected because the developers are overwhelmingly white and male: among AI engineers, about 4% are black and 20% are women.<sup about="#mwt1000" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995_271-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995-271&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;995&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021995-271" id="mwB2Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB2U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2Y">[</span>258<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB2c">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB2g">There are various conflicting definitions and mathematical models of fairness. These notions depend on ethical assumptions, and are influenced by beliefs about society. One broad category is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distributive_justice" title="Distributive justice" id="mwB2k">distributive fairness</a>, which focuses on the outcomes, often identifying groups and seeking to compensate for statistical disparities. Representational fairness tries to ensure that AI systems do not reinforce negative <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereotype" title="Stereotype" id="mwB2o">stereotypes</a> or render certain groups invisible. Procedural fairness focuses on the decision process rather than the outcome. The most relevant notions of fairness may depend on the context, notably the type of AI application and the stakeholders. The subjectivity in the notions of bias and fairness makes it difficult for companies to operationalise them. Having access to sensitive attributes such as race or gender is also considered by many AI ethicists to be necessary in order to compensate for biases, but it may conflict with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-discrimination_law" title="Anti-discrimination law" id="mwB2s">anti-discrimination laws</a>.<sup about="#mwt1005" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Samuel-2022_263-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Samuel-2022&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Samuel-2022-263&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Samuel-2022-263" id="mwB2w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB20"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB24">[</span>251<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB28">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB3A">At the 2022 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACM_Conference_on_Fairness,_Accountability,_and_Transparency" title="ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency" id="mwB3E">ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency</a> a paper reported that a CLIP‑based (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contrastive_Language-Image_Pre-training" title="Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB3I">Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training</a>) robotic system reproduced harmful gender‑ and race‑linked stereotypes in a simulated manipulation task. The authors recommended robot‑learning methods which physically manifest such harms be "paused, reworked, or even wound down when appropriate, until outcomes can be proven safe, effective, and just."<sup about="#mwt1008" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-282" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-282&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-282" id="mwB3M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3U">[</span>267<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3Y">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1011" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-283" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-283&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-283" id="mwB3c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3k">[</span>268<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB3o">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1014" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-284" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-284&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-284" id="mwB3s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB3w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB30">[</span>269<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB34">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="42" id="mwB38" aria-labelledby="Lack_of_transparency"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Lack_of_transparency">Lack of transparency</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1015" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB4A" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Explainable AI&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Algorithmic transparency&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Right to explanation&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1016" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1015" id="mwB4E">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explainable_AI" title="Explainable AI" class="mw-redirect">Explainable AI</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithmic_transparency" title="Algorithmic transparency">Algorithmic transparency</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_explanation" title="Right to explanation">Right to explanation</a></div>
<p id="mwB4I">Many AI systems are so complex that their designers cannot explain how they reach their decisions.<sup about="#mwt1017" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESample2017_285-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESample2017&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESample2017-285&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sample&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2017&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESample2017-285" id="mwB4M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4U">[</span>270<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4Y">]</span></span></a></sup> Particularly with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_neural_networks" title="Deep neural networks" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB4c">deep neural networks</a>, in which there are many non-<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear" title="Linear" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB4g">linear</a> relationships between inputs and outputs. But some popular explainability techniques exist.<sup about="#mwt1022" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-286" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-286&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-286" id="mwB4k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB4o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4s">[</span>271<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB4w">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB40">It is impossible to be certain that a program is operating correctly if no one knows how exactly it works. There have been many cases where a machine learning program passed rigorous tests, but nevertheless learned something different than what the programmers intended. For example, a system that could identify skin diseases better than medical professionals was found to actually have a strong tendency to classify images with a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruler" title="Ruler" id="mwB44">ruler</a> as "cancerous", because pictures of malignancies typically include a ruler to show the scale.<sup about="#mwt1023" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian2020110_287-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian2020110&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian2020110-287&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;110&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian2020110-287" id="mwB48"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB5A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5E">[</span>272<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5I">]</span></span></a></sup> Another machine learning system designed to help effectively allocate medical resources was found to classify patients with asthma as being at "low risk" of dying from pneumonia. Having asthma is actually a severe risk factor, but since the patients having asthma would usually get much more medical care, they were relatively unlikely to die according to the training data. The correlation between asthma and low risk of dying from pneumonia was real, but misleading.<sup about="#mwt1026" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian202088–91_288-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian202088–91&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202088–91-288&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;88–91&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202088–91-288" id="mwB5M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB5Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5U">[</span>273<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5Y">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB5c">People who have been harmed by an algorithm's decision have a right to an explanation.<sup about="#mwt1037" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-289" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-289&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-289" id="mwB5g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB5k"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5o">[</span>274<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB5s">]</span></span></a></sup> Doctors, for example, are expected to clearly and completely explain to their colleagues the reasoning behind any decision they make. Early drafts of the European Union's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Data_Protection_Regulation" title="General Data Protection Regulation" id="mwB5w">General Data Protection Regulation</a> in 2016 included an explicit statement that this right exists.<sup about="#mwt1029" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-290" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-290&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;When the law was passed in 2018, it still contained a form of this provision.&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-290" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwB50"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB54"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB58">[</span>p<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6A">]</span></span></a></sup> Industry experts noted that this is an unsolved problem with no solution in sight. Regulators argued that nevertheless the harm is real: if the problem has no solution, the tools should not be used.<sup about="#mwt1032" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian202091_291-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian202091&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202091-291&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;91&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202091-291" id="mwB6E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB6I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6M">[</span>275<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB6U"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA" title="DARPA" id="mwB6Y">DARPA</a> established the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explainable_Artificial_Intelligence" title="Explainable Artificial Intelligence" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB6c">XAI</a> ("Explainable Artificial Intelligence") program in 2014 to try to solve these problems.<sup about="#mwt1038" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian202083_292-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian202083&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202083-292&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;83&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202083-292" id="mwB6g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB6k"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6o">[</span>276<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB6s">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB6w">Several approaches aim to address the transparency problem. SHAP enables to visualise the contribution of each feature to the output.<sup about="#mwt1041" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEVerma2021_293-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEVerma2021&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEVerma2021-293&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Verma&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVerma2021-293" id="mwB60"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB64"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB68">[</span>277<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7A">]</span></span></a></sup> LIME can locally approximate a model's outputs with a simpler, interpretable model.<sup about="#mwt1044" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERothman2020_294-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERothman2020&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERothman2020-294&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Rothman&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERothman2020-294" id="mwB7E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB7I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7M">[</span>278<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7Q">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multitask_learning" title="Multitask learning" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB7U">Multitask learning</a> provides a large number of outputs in addition to the target classification. These other outputs can help developers deduce what the network has learned.<sup about="#mwt1047" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian2020105–108_295-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian2020105–108&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian2020105–108-295&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;105–108&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian2020105–108-295" id="mwB7Y"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB7c"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7g">[</span>279<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB7k">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deconvolution" title="Deconvolution" id="mwB7o">Deconvolution</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepDream" title="DeepDream" id="mwB7s">DeepDream</a> and other <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI" title="Generative AI" id="mwB7w">generative</a> methods can allow developers to see what different layers of a deep network for computer vision have learned, and produce output that can suggest what the network is learning.<sup about="#mwt1050" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian2020108–112_296-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian2020108–112&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian2020108–112-296&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;108–112&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian2020108–112-296" id="mwB70"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB74"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB78">[</span>280<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8A">]</span></span></a></sup> For <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_pre-trained_transformer" title="Generative pre-trained transformer" id="mwB8E">generative pre-trained transformers</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic" title="Anthropic" id="mwB8I">Anthropic</a> developed a technique based on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dictionary_learning" title="Dictionary learning" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB8M">dictionary learning</a> that associates patterns of neuron activations with human-understandable concepts.<sup about="#mwt1055" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-297" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-297&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-297" id="mwB8Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB8U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8Y">[</span>281<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB8c">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="43" id="mwB8g" aria-labelledby="Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Bad_actors_and_weaponised_AI">Bad actors and weaponised AI</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1056" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwB8k" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Lethal autonomous weapon&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Artificial intelligence arms race&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;AI safety&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1057" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1056" id="mwB8o">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lethal_autonomous_weapon" title="Lethal autonomous weapon">Lethal autonomous weapon</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_arms_race" title="Artificial intelligence arms race">Artificial intelligence arms race</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_safety" title="AI safety">AI safety</a></div>

<p id="mwB8s">Artificial intelligence provides a number of tools that are useful to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_actor" title="Bad actor" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB8w">bad actors</a>, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authoritarian" title="Authoritarian" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB80">authoritarian governments</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrorist" title="Terrorist" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB84">terrorists</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminals" title="Criminals" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB88">criminals</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_states" title="Rogue states" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB9A">rogue states</a>.</p>

<p id="mwB9E">A lethal autonomous weapon is a machine that locates, selects and engages human targets without human supervision.<sup about="#mwt1058" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-299" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-299&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;This is the [[United Nations]]' definition, and includes things like [[land mines]] as well.{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=989}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-299" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwB9I"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB9M"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9Q">[</span>q<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9U">]</span></span></a></sup> Widely available AI tools can be used by bad actors to develop inexpensive autonomous weapons and, if produced at scale, they are potentially <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weapons_of_mass_destruction" title="Weapons of mass destruction" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB9Y">weapons of mass destruction</a>.<sup about="#mwt1064" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990_300-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990-300&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;987–990&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990-300" id="mwB9c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB9g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9k">[</span>283<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB9o">]</span></span></a></sup> Even when used in conventional warfare, they currently cannot reliably choose targets and could potentially <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder" title="Murder" id="mwB9s">kill an innocent person</a>.<sup about="#mwt1067" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990_300-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990-300&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;987–990&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021987–990-300" id="mwB9w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB90"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB94">[</span>283<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB98">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2014, 30 nations (including China) supported a ban on autonomous weapons under the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations" id="mwB-A">United Nations</a>' <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_on_Certain_Conventional_Weapons" title="Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons" id="mwB-E">Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons</a>, however the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States" title="United States" id="mwB-I">United
