States</a> and others disagreed.<sup about="#mwt1070" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021988_301-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021988&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021988-301&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;988&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021988-301" id="mwB-M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB-Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-U">[</span>284<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-Y">]</span></span></a></sup> By 2015, over fifty countries were reported to be researching battlefield robots.<sup about="#mwt1075" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-302" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-302&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-302" id="mwB-c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB-g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-k">[</span>285<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB-o">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwB-s">AI tools make it easier for authoritarian governments to efficiently control their citizens in several ways. Face and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_recognition" title="Speaker recognition" id="mwB-w">voice recognition</a> allow widespread <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surveillance" title="Surveillance" id="mwB-0">surveillance</a>. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mwB-4">Machine learning</a>, operating this data, can <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classifier_(machine_learning)" title="Classifier (machine learning)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB-8">classify</a> potential enemies of the state and prevent them from hiding. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recommendation_systems" title="Recommendation systems" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB_A">Recommendation systems</a> can precisely target <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propaganda" title="Propaganda" id="mwB_E">propaganda</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misinformation" title="Misinformation" id="mwB_I">misinformation</a> for maximum effect. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepfakes" title="Deepfakes" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB_M">Deepfakes</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI" title="Generative AI" id="mwB_Q">generative AI</a> aid in producing misinformation. Advanced AI can make authoritarian <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technocracy" title="Technocracy" id="mwB_U">centralised decision-making</a> more competitive than liberal and decentralised systems such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_(economics)" title="Market (economics)" id="mwB_Y">markets</a>. It lowers the cost and difficulty of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_warfare" title="Digital warfare" class="mw-redirect" id="mwB_c">digital warfare</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spyware" title="Spyware" id="mwB_g">advanced spyware</a>.<sup about="#mwt1076" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHarari2018_303-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHarari2018&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarari2018-303&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Harari&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2018&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarari2018-303" id="mwB_k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwB_o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_s">[</span>286<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwB_w">]</span></span></a></sup> All these technologies have been available since 2020 or earlier—AI <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_recognition_system" title="Facial recognition system" id="mwB_0">facial recognition systems</a> are already being used for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_surveillance" title="Mass surveillance" id="mwB_4">mass surveillance</a> in China.<sup about="#mwt1081" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-304" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-304&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-304" id="mwB_8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCAA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAE">[</span>287<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAI">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1084" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-305" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-305&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-305" id="mwCAM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCAQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAU">[</span>288<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCAc">There are many other ways in which AI is expected to help bad actors, some of which can not be foreseen. For example, machine-learning AI is able to design tens of thousands of toxic molecules in a matter of hours.<sup about="#mwt1085" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEUrbinaLentzosInvernizziEkins2022_306-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEUrbinaLentzosInvernizziEkins2022&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEUrbinaLentzosInvernizziEkins2022-306&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Urbina&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Lentzos&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Invernizzi&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Ekins&quot;},&quot;5&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2022&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUrbinaLentzosInvernizziEkins2022-306" id="mwCAg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCAk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAo">[</span>289<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCAs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="44" id="mwCAw" aria-labelledby="Technological_unemployment"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Technological_unemployment">Technological unemployment</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1088" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCA0" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Workplace impact of artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Technological unemployment&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1089" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1088" id="mwCA4">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workplace_impact_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Workplace impact of artificial intelligence">Workplace impact of artificial intelligence</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technological_unemployment" title="Technological unemployment">Technological unemployment</a></div>

<p id="mwCA8">Economists have frequently highlighted the risks of redundancies from AI, and speculated about unemployment if there is no adequate social policy for full employment.<sup about="#mwt1090" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMcGaughey2022_307-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMcGaughey2022&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGaughey2022-307&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;McGaughey&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2022&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGaughey2022-307" id="mwCBA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCBE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBI">[</span>290<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- TOPIC: ESTIMATES OF THE AMOUNT OF UNEMPLOYMENT -->
<p id="mwCBQ">In the past, technology has tended to increase rather than reduce total employment, but economists acknowledge that "we're in uncharted territory" with AI.<sup about="#mwt1107" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-308" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-308&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-308" id="mwCBU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCBY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBc">[</span>291<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCBg">]</span></span></a></sup> A survey of economists showed disagreement about whether the increasing use of robots and AI will cause a substantial increase in long-term <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment" title="Unemployment" id="mwCBk">unemployment</a>, but they generally agree that it could be a net benefit if <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productivity" title="Productivity" id="mwCBo">productivity</a> gains are <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redistribution_of_income_and_wealth" title="Redistribution of income and wealth" id="mwCBs">redistributed</a>.<sup about="#mwt1093" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEIGM_Chicago2017_309-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEIGM Chicago2017&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEIGM_Chicago2017-309&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;IGM Chicago&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2017&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIGM_Chicago2017-309" id="mwCBw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCB0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCB4">[</span>292<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCB8">]</span></span></a></sup> Risk estimates vary; for example, in the 2010s, Michael Osborne and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Benedikt_Frey" title="Carl Benedikt Frey" id="mwCCA">Carl Benedikt Frey</a> estimated 47% of U.S. jobs are at "high risk" of potential automation, while an OECD report classified only 9% of U.S. jobs as "high risk".<sup about="#mwt1096" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-311" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-311&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See table 4; 9% is both the OECD average and the U.S. average.{{Sfnp|Arntz|Gregory|Zierahn|2016|p=33}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-311" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCCE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCCI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCM">[</span>r<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1111" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-312" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-312&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-312" id="mwCCU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCCY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCc">[</span>294<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCCg">]</span></span></a></sup> The methodology of speculating about future employment levels has been criticised as lacking evidential foundation, and for implying that technology, rather than social policy, creates unemployment, as opposed to redundancies.<sup about="#mwt1102" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMcGaughey2022_307-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMcGaughey2022&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcGaughey2022-307&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;McGaughey&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2022&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a id="mwCCw">]</span></span></a></sup> In April 2023, it was reported that 70% of the jobs for Chinese video game illustrators had been eliminated by generative artificial intelligence.<sup about="#mwt1114" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-313" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" id="cite_ref-314" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employment_rate" title="Employment rate" id="mwCDU">employment rates</a> in some AI-exposed occupations.<sup about="#mwt1120" class="mw-ref data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;o861&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-o861-315&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-o861-315" id="mwCDY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCDc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCDg">[</span>297<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCDk">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- TOPIC: WHICH JOBS ARE AT RISK? -->
<p id="mwCDo">Unlike previous waves of automation, many middle-class jobs may be eliminated by artificial intelligence; <i id="mwCDs"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Economist" title="The Economist" id="mwCDw">The Economist</a></i> stated in 2015 that "the worry that AI could do to white-collar jobs what steam power did to blue-collar ones during the Industrial Revolution" is "worth taking seriously".<sup about="#mwt1121" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMorgenstern2015_316-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMorgenstern2015&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorgenstern2015-316&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Morgenstern&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2015&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorgenstern2015-316" id="mwCD0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCD4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCD8">[</span>298<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEA">]</span></span></a></sup> Jobs at extreme risk range from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralegal" title="Paralegal" id="mwCEE">paralegals</a> to fast food cooks, while job demand is likely to increase for care-related professions ranging from personal healthcare to the clergy.<sup about="#mwt1126" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-317" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-317&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-317" id="mwCEI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCEM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEQ">[</span>299<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEU">]</span></span></a></sup> In July 2025, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company" title="Ford Motor Company" id="mwCEY">Ford</a> CEO <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Farley_(businessman)" title="Jim Farley (businessman)" id="mwCEc">Jim Farley</a> predicted that "artificial intelligence is going to replace literally half of all <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-collar_worker" title="White-collar worker" id="mwCEg">white-collar workers</a> in the U.S."<sup about="#mwt1129" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-318" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-318&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-318" id="mwCEk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCEo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEs">[</span>300<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCEw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCE0">From the early days of the development of artificial intelligence, there have been arguments, for example, those put forward by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Weizenbaum" title="Joseph Weizenbaum" id="mwCE4">Joseph Weizenbaum</a>, who developed the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA" title="ELIZA" id="mwCE8">ELIZA</a> chatbot between 1964 and 1966, about whether tasks that can be done by computers actually should be done by them, given the difference between computers and humans, and between quantitative calculation and qualitative, value-based judgement.<sup about="#mwt1132" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-319" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-319&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-319" id="mwCFA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCFE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFI">[</span>301<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="45" id="mwCFQ" aria-labelledby="Substitution_for_human–human_interaction"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Substitution_for_human–human_interaction"><span id="Substitution_for_human.E2.80.93human_interaction" typeof="mw:FallbackId"></span>Substitution for human–human interaction</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1133" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCFU" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;see also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Deaths linked to chatbots&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1134" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1133" id="mwCFY">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deaths_linked_to_chatbots" title="Deaths linked to chatbots">Deaths linked to chatbots</a></div>
<p id="mwCFc">With the increase of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loneliness#increasing_prevalence" title="Loneliness" id="mwCFg">loneliness</a> in the early 21st century, AI is sometimes identified as a potential source of relief to this problem. It would be possible, via <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_anthropomorphism#Current_anthropomorphic_attributions" title="AI anthropomorphism" id="mwCFk">human-like qualities built into AI products</a>,<sup about="#mwt1137" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Anthropomorphism_320-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Anthropomorphism&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Anthropomorphism-320&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Anthropomorphism-320" id="mwCFo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCFs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCFw">[</span>302<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCF0">]</span></span></a></sup> for individuals to assume that this need can be met by artificial means.<sup about="#mwt1140" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-ReevesNass1996_321-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ReevesNass1996&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ReevesNass1996-321&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-ReevesNass1996-321" id="mwCF4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCF8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGA">[</span>303<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGE">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1143" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-NassMoon2000_322-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NassMoon2000&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NassMoon2000-322&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-NassMoon2000-322" id="mwCGI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGQ">[</span>304<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGU">]</span></span></a></sup> In some cases, people approach artificial intelligence for companionship when they believe that they would not find acceptance due to feeling outcast.<sup about="#mwt1146" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-323" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-323&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-323" id="mwCGY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCGc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGg">[</span>305<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCGk">]</span></span></a></sup> Examples of harm coming to humans from advanced <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatbots" title="Chatbots" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCGo">chatbots</a> have been reported in courts in the United States, with AI companies accused of creating products that endanger humans through <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illusion_of_understanding" title="Illusion of understanding" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCGs">emotional confusion or deception</a>.<sup about="#mwt1149" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-324" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-324&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-324" id="mwCGw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCG0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCG4">[</span>306<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCG8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1152" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-325" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-325&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-325" id="mwCHA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCHE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHI">[</span>307<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHM">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="46" id="mwCHQ" aria-labelledby="Existential_risk"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Existential_risk">Existential risk</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1153" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCHU" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Existential risk from artificial intelligence&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1154" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1153" id="mwCHY">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Existential_risk_from_artificial_intelligence" title="Existential risk from artificial intelligence">Existential risk from artificial intelligence</a></div>

<p id="mwCHc">Recent public debates in artificial intelligence have increasingly focused on its broader societal and ethical implications. It has been argued AI will become so powerful that humanity may irreversibly lose control of it. This could, as physicist <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Hawking" title="Stephen Hawking" id="mwCHg">Stephen Hawking</a> stated, "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_catastrophic_risk" title="Global catastrophic risk" id="mwCHk">spell the end of the human race</a>".<sup about="#mwt1155" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECellan-Jones2014_326-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECellan-Jones2014&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECellan-Jones2014-326&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Cellan-Jones&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2014&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECellan-Jones2014-326" id="mwCHo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCHs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCHw">[</span>308<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCH0">]</span></span></a></sup> This scenario has been common in science fiction, when a computer or robot suddenly develops a human-like "self-awareness" (or "sentience" or "consciousness") and becomes a malevolent character.<sup about="#mwt1158" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-328" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-328&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sometimes called a \&quot;[[robopocalypse]]\&quot;{{Sfn|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=1001}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-328" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCH4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCH8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIA">[</span>s<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIE">]</span></span></a></sup> These sci-fi scenarios are misleading in several ways.</p>

<!-- Unnecessary sentience -->
<p id="mwCII">First, AI does not require human-like <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentience" title="Sentience" id="mwCIM">sentience</a> to be an existential risk. Modern AI programs are given specific goals and use learning and intelligence to achieve them. Philosopher <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Bostrom" title="Nick Bostrom" id="mwCIQ">Nick Bostrom</a> argued that if one gives <i id="mwCIU">almost any</i> goal to a sufficiently powerful AI, it may choose to destroy humanity to achieve it (he used the example of an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instrumental_convergence#Paperclip_maximizer" title="Instrumental convergence" id="mwCIY">automated paperclip factory</a> that destroys the world to get more iron for paperclips).<sup about="#mwt1164" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBostrom2014_329-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEBostrom2014&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEBostrom2014-329&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Bostrom&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2014&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBostrom2014-329" id="mwCIc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCIg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIk">[</span>310<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCIo">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_J._Russell" title="Stuart J. Russell" id="mwCIs">Stuart Russell</a> gives the example of household robot that tries to find a way to kill its owner to prevent it from being unplugged, reasoning that "you can't fetch the coffee if you're dead."<sup about="#mwt1167" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussell2019_330-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussell2019&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussell2019-330&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2019&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussell2019-330" id="mwCIw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCI0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCI4">[</span>311<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCI8">]</span></span></a></sup> In order to be safe for humanity, a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superintelligence" title="Superintelligence" id="mwCJA">superintelligence</a> would have to be genuinely <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_alignment" title="AI alignment" id="mwCJE">aligned</a> with humanity's morality and values so that it is "fundamentally on our side".<sup about="#mwt1173" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-331" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-331&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-331" id="mwCJI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCJM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCJQ">[</span>312<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCJU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- Acting in the world is unnecessary -->
<p id="mwCJY">Second, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuval_Noah_Harari" title="Yuval Noah Harari" id="mwCJc">Yuval Noah Harari</a> argues that AI does not require a robot body or physical control to pose an existential risk. The essential parts of civilisation are not physical. Things like <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ideologies" title="Ideologies" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCJg">ideologies</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law" title="Law" id="mwCJk">law</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government" title="Government" id="mwCJo">government</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money" title="Money" id="mwCJs">money</a> and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy" title="Economy" id="mwCJw">economy</a> are built on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language" title="Language" id="mwCJ0">language</a>; they exist because there are stories that billions of people believe. The current prevalence of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misinformation" title="Misinformation" id="mwCJ4">misinformation</a> suggests that an AI could use language to convince people to believe anything, even to take actions that are destructive.<sup about="#mwt1174" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHarari2023_332-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHarari2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarari2023-332&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Harari&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarari2023-332" id="mwCJ8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCKA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKE">[</span>313<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKI">]</span></span></a></sup> Geoffrey Hinton said in 2025 that <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model" title="Large language model" id="mwCKM">modern AI</a> is particularly "good at persuasion" and getting better all the time. He asks, "Suppose you wanted to invade the capital of the US. Do you have to go there and do it yourself? No. You just have to be good at persuasion."<sup about="#mwt1177" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEStewart2025_333-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEStewart2025&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEStewart2025-333&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Stewart&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2025&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStewart2025-333" id="mwCKQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCKU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKY">[</span>314<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- Warnings of existential risk -->
<p id="mwCKg">The opinions amongst experts and industry insiders are mixed, with sizeable fractions both concerned and unconcerned by risk from eventual superintelligent AI.<sup about="#mwt1180" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMüllerBostrom2014_334-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMüllerBostrom2014&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMüllerBostrom2014-334&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Müller&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Bostrom&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2014&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMüllerBostrom2014-334" id="mwCKk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCKo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKs">[</span>315<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCKw">]</span></span></a></sup> Personalities such as Stephen Hawking, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates" title="Bill Gates" id="mwCK0">Bill Gates</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk" title="Elon Musk" id="mwCK4">Elon Musk</a>,<sup about="#mwt1187" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-335" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-335&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-335" id="mwCK8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCLA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLE">[</span>316<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLI">]</span></span></a></sup> as well as AI pioneers such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton" title="Geoffrey Hinton" id="mwCLM">Geoffrey Hinton</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshua_Bengio" title="Yoshua Bengio" id="mwCLQ">Yoshua Bengio</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_J._Russell" title="Stuart J. Russell" id="mwCLU">Stuart Russell</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demis_Hassabis" title="Demis Hassabis" id="mwCLY">Demis Hassabis</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Altman" title="Sam Altman" id="mwCLc">Sam Altman</a>, have expressed concerns about existential risk from AI.</p>

<p id="mwCLg">In May 2023, Geoffrey Hinton announced his resignation from Google in order to be able to "freely speak out about the risks of AI" without "considering how this impacts Google".<sup about="#mwt1190" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-336" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-336&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-336" id="mwCLk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCLo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLs">[</span>317<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCLw">]</span></span></a></sup> He notably mentioned risks of an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_takeover" title="AI takeover" id="mwCL0">AI takeover</a>,<sup about="#mwt1193" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-337" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-337&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-337" id="mwCL4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCL8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMA">[</span>318<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCME">]</span></span></a></sup> and stressed that in order to avoid the worst outcomes, establishing safety guidelines will require cooperation among those competing in use of AI.<sup about="#mwt1196" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-338" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-338&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-338" id="mwCMI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCMM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMQ">[</span>319<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCMY">In 2023, many leading AI experts endorsed <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statement_on_AI_risk_of_extinction" title="Statement on AI risk of extinction" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCMc">the joint statement</a> that "Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war".<sup about="#mwt1197" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEValance2023_339-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEValance2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEValance2023-339&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Valance&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEValance2023-339" id="mwCMg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCMk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMo">[</span>320<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCMs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- Arguments against existential risk -->
<p id="mwCMw">Some other researchers were more optimistic. AI pioneer <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jürgen_Schmidhuber" title="Jürgen Schmidhuber" id="mwCM0">Jürgen Schmidhuber</a> did not sign the joint statement, emphasising that in 95% of all cases, AI research is about making "human lives longer and healthier and easier."<sup about="#mwt1205" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-340" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-340&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-340" id="mwCM4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCM8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNA">[</span>321<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNE">]</span></span></a></sup> While the tools that are now being used to improve lives can also be used by bad actors, "they can also be used against the bad actors."<sup about="#mwt1208" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-341" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-341&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-341" id="mwCNI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCNM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNQ">[</span>322<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1211" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-342" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-342&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-342" id="mwCNY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCNc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNg">[</span>323<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCNk">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Ng" title="Andrew Ng" id="mwCNo">Andrew Ng</a> also argued that "it's a mistake to fall for the doomsday hype on AI—and that regulators who do will only benefit vested interests."<sup about="#mwt1214" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-343" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-343&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-343" id="mwCNs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCNw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCN0">[</span>324<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCN4">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yann_LeCun" title="Yann LeCun" id="mwCN8">Yann LeCun</a>, a Turing Award winner, disagreed with the idea that AI will subordinate humans "simply because they are smarter, let alone destroy [us]",<sup about="#mwt1217" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-344" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-344&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-344" id="mwCOA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCOE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOI">[</span>325<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOM">]</span></span></a></sup> "scoff[ing] at his peers' dystopian scenarios of supercharged misinformation and even, eventually, human extinction." In contrast, he claimed that "intelligent machines will usher in a new renaissance for humanity, a new era of enlightenment."<sup about="#mwt1220" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-345" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-345&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-345" id="mwCOQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCOU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOY">[</span>326<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOc">]</span></span></a></sup> In the early 2010s, experts argued that the risks are too distant in the future to warrant research or that humans will be valuable from the perspective of a superintelligent machine.<sup about="#mwt1225" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-346" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-346&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-346" id="mwCOg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCOk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOo">[</span>327<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCOs">]</span></span></a></sup> However, after 2016, the study of current and future risks and possible solutions became a serious area of research.<sup about="#mwt1200" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian202067,_73_347-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian202067, 73&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202067,_73-347&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;67, 73&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202067,_73-347" id="mwCOw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCO0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCO4">[</span>328<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCO8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="47" id="mwCPA" aria-labelledby="Ethical_machines_and_alignment"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Ethical_machines_and_alignment">Ethical machines and alignment</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1226" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCPE" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Machine ethics&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;AI safety&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Friendly artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Artificial moral agents&quot;},&quot;5&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Human Compatible&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1227" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1226" id="mwCPI">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_ethics" title="Machine ethics">Machine ethics</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_safety" title="AI safety">AI safety</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendly_artificial_intelligence" title="Friendly artificial intelligence">Friendly artificial intelligence</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_moral_agents" title="Artificial moral agents" class="mw-redirect">Artificial moral agents</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Compatible" title="Human Compatible">Human Compatible</a></div>

<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1228" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCPM" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Human–AI interaction&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1229" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1228" id="mwCPQ">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human–AI_interaction" title="Human–AI interaction">Human–AI interaction</a></div>
<p id="mwCPU">Friendly AI are machines that have been designed from the beginning to minimise risks and to make choices that benefit humans. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky" title="Eliezer Yudkowsky" id="mwCPY">Eliezer Yudkowsky</a>, who coined the term, argues that developing friendly AI should be a higher research priority: it may require a large investment and it must be completed before AI becomes an existential risk.<sup about="#mwt1230" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEYudkowsky2008_348-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEYudkowsky2008&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEYudkowsky2008-348&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Yudkowsky&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2008&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEYudkowsky2008-348" id="mwCPc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCPg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPk">[</span>329<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCPo">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCPs">Machines with intelligence have the potential to use their intelligence to make ethical decisions. The field of machine ethics provides machines with ethical principles and procedures for resolving ethical dilemmas.<sup about="#mwt1233" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011_349-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011-349&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Anderson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Anderson&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2011&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011-349" id="mwCPw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCP0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCP4">[</span>330<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCP8">]</span></span></a></sup>
The field of machine ethics is also called computational morality,<sup about="#mwt1236" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011_349-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011-349&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Anderson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Anderson&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2011&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAndersonAnderson2011-349" id="mwCQA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCQE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQI">[</span>330<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQM">]</span></span></a></sup>
and was founded at an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAAI" title="AAAI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCQQ">AAAI</a> symposium in 2005.<sup about="#mwt1239" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAAAI2014_350-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEAAAI2014&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEAAAI2014-350&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;AAAI&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2014&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAAAI2014-350" id="mwCQU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCQY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQc">[</span>331<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCQk">Other approaches include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendell_Wallach" title="Wendell Wallach" id="mwCQo">Wendell Wallach</a>'s "artificial moral agents"<sup about="#mwt1242" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEWallach2010_351-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEWallach2010&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEWallach2010-351&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Wallach&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2010&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWallach2010-351" id="mwCQs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCQw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQ0">[</span>332<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQ4">]</span></span></a></sup> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_J._Russell" title="Stuart J. Russell" id="mwCQ8">Stuart J. Russell</a>'s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Compatible#Russell's_three_principles" title="Human Compatible" id="mwCRA">three principles</a> for developing provably beneficial machines.<sup about="#mwt1245" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussell2019173_352-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussell2019173&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussell2019173-352&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2019&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;173&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussell2019173-352" id="mwCRE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCRI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRM">[</span>333<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="48" id="mwCRU" aria-labelledby="Open_source"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Open_source">Open source</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1248" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCRY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Open-source artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Lists of open-source artificial intelligence software&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1249" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1248" id="mwCRc">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_artificial_intelligence" title="Open-source artificial intelligence">Open-source artificial intelligence</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lists_of_open-source_artificial_intelligence_software" title="Lists of open-source artificial intelligence software">Lists of open-source artificial intelligence software</a></div>
<p id="mwCRg">Active organisations in the AI open-source community include <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugging_Face" title="Hugging Face" id="mwCRk">Hugging Face</a>,<sup about="#mwt1252" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-353" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-353&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-353" id="mwCRo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCRs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCRw">[</span>334<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCR0">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google" title="Google" id="mwCR4">Google</a>,<sup about="#mwt1255" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-354" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-354&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-354" id="mwCR8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCSA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCSE">[</span>335<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCSI">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EleutherAI" title="EleutherAI" id="mwCSM">EleutherAI</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms" title="Meta Platforms" id="mwCSQ">Meta</a>.<sup about="#mwt1258" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-355" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-355&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-355" id="mwCSU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCSY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCSc">[</span>336<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCSg">]</span></span></a></sup> Various AI models, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LLaMA" title="LLaMA" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCSk">Llama 2</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_AI" title="Mistral AI" id="mwCSo">Mistral</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_Diffusion" title="Stable Diffusion" id="mwCSs">Stable Diffusion</a>, have been made open-weight,<sup about="#mwt1261" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-356" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-356&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-356" id="mwCSw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCS0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCS4">[</span>337<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCS8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1264" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-357" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-357&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-357" id="mwCTA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCTE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCTI">[</span>338<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCTM">]</span></span></a></sup> meaning that their architecture and trained parameters (the "weights") are publicly available. Open-weight models can be freely <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine-tuning_(deep_learning)" title="Fine-tuning (deep learning)" id="mwCTQ">fine-tuned</a>, which allows companies to specialise them with their own data and for their own use-case.<sup about="#mwt1267" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-358" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-358&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-358" id="mwCTU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCTY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCTc">[</span>339<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCTg">]</span></span></a></sup> Open-weight models are useful for research and innovation but can also be misused. Since they can be fine-tuned, any built-in security measure, such as objecting to harmful requests, can be trained away until it becomes ineffective. Some researchers warn that future AI models may develop dangerous capabilities (such as the potential to drastically facilitate <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioterrorism" title="Bioterrorism" id="mwCTk">bioterrorism</a>) and that once released on the Internet, they cannot be deleted everywhere if needed. They recommend pre-release audits and cost-benefit analyses.<sup about="#mwt1270" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-359" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-359&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-359" id="mwCTo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCTs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCTw">[</span>340<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCT0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="49" id="mwCT4" aria-labelledby="Frameworks"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Frameworks">Frameworks</h3></div>
<p id="mwCT8">Artificial intelligence projects can be guided by ethical considerations during the design, development, and implementation of an AI system. An AI framework such as the Care and Act Framework, developed by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Turing_Institute" title="Alan Turing Institute" id="mwCUA">Alan Turing Institute</a> and based on the SUM values, outlines four main ethical dimensions, defined as follows:<sup about="#mwt1273" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-360" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-360&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-360" id="mwCUE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCUI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCUM">[</span>341<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCUQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1276" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-361" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-361&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-361" id="mwCUU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCUY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCUc">[</span>342<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCUg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<ul id="mwCUk"><li id="mwCUo"><b id="mwCUs">Respect</b> the dignity of individual people</li>
<li id="mwCUw"><b id="mwCU0">Connect</b> with other people sincerely, openly, and inclusively</li>
<li id="mwCU4"><b id="mwCU8">Care</b> for the wellbeing of everyone</li>
<li id="mwCVA"><b id="mwCVE">Protect</b> social values, justice, and the public interest</li></ul>

<p id="mwCVI">Other developments in ethical frameworks include those decided upon during the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asilomar_Conference_on_Beneficial_AI" title="Asilomar Conference on Beneficial AI" id="mwCVM">Asilomar Conference</a>, the Montreal Declaration for Responsible AI, and the IEEE's Ethics of Autonomous Systems initiative, among others;<sup about="#mwt1279" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-362" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-362&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-362" id="mwCVQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCVU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVY">[</span>343<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVc">]</span></span></a></sup> however, these principles are not without criticism, especially regarding the people chosen to contribute to these frameworks.<sup about="#mwt1282" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-363" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-363&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-363" id="mwCVg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCVk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVo">[</span>344<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCVs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCVw">Promotion of the wellbeing of the people and communities that these technologies affect requires consideration of the social and ethical implications at all stages of AI system design, development and implementation, and collaboration between job roles such as data scientists, product managers, data engineers, domain experts, and delivery managers.<sup about="#mwt1285" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-364" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-364&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-364" id="mwCV0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCV4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCV8">[</span>345<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCWE">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_Safety_Institute_(United_Kingdom)" title="AI Safety Institute (United Kingdom)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCWI">UK AI Safety Institute</a> released in 2024 a testing toolset called 'Inspect' for AI safety evaluations available under an MIT open-source licence which is freely available on GitHub and can be improved with third-party packages. It can be used to evaluate AI models in a range of areas including core knowledge, ability to reason, and autonomous capabilities.<sup about="#mwt1288" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-365" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-365&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-365" id="mwCWM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCWQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWU">[</span>346<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCWY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="50" id="mwCWc" aria-labelledby="Regulation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Regulation">Regulation</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1289" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCWg" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Regulation of artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Regulation of algorithms&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;AI safety&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1290" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1289" id="mwCWk">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Regulation of artificial intelligence">Regulation of artificial intelligence</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_of_algorithms" title="Regulation of algorithms">Regulation of algorithms</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_safety" title="AI safety">AI safety</a></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCWo"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vice_President_Harris_at_the_group_photo_of_the_2023_AI_Safety_Summit.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCWs"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vice_President_Harris_at_the_group_photo_of_the_2023_AI_Safety_Summit.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Vice_President_Harris_at_the_group_photo_of_the_2023_AI_Safety_Summit.jpg/330px-Vice_President_Harris_at_the_group_photo_of_the_2023_AI_Safety_Summit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Vice_President_Harris_at_the_group_photo_of_the_2023_AI_Safety_Summit.jpg/960px-Vice_President_Harris_at_the_group_photo_of_the_2023_AI_Safety_Summit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" alt="AI Safety Summit" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1369" data-file-type="bitmap" height="201" width="300" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.2" id="mwCWw"></a><figcaption id="mwCW0">The first global <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_Safety_Summit_2023" title="AI Safety Summit 2023" id="mwCW4">AI Safety Summit</a> was held in the United Kingdom in November 2023 with a declaration calling for international cooperation.</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwCW8">The regulation of artificial intelligence is the development of public sector policies and laws for promoting and regulating AI; it is therefore related to the broader regulation of algorithms.<sup about="#mwt1320" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-366" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-366&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-366" id="mwCXA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCXE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCXI">[</span>347<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCXM">]</span></span></a></sup> The regulatory and policy landscape for AI is an emerging issue in jurisdictions globally.<sup about="#mwt1291" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELaw_Library_of_Congress_(U.S.)._Global_Legal_Research_Directorate2019_367-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELaw Library of Congress (U.S.). Global Legal Research Directorate&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2019&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELaw_Library_of_Congress_(U.S.)._Global_Legal_Research_Directorate2019-367" id="mwCXQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCXU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCXY">[</span>348<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCXc">]</span></span></a></sup> According to AI Index at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford" title="Stanford" Federation, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, U.S., and Vietnam. Others were in the process of elaborating their own AI strategy, including Bangladesh, Malaysia and Tunisia.<sup about="#mwt1303" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEUNESCO2021_370-1" href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUNESCO2021-370" id="mwCYs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCYw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCY0">[</span>351<span class="cite-bracket" about="#mwt1312" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAltmanBrockmanSutskever2023_372-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" &quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAltmanBrockmanSutskever2023-372" id="mwCZY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCZc"><span href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe" id="mwCaM">Council of Europe</a> created the first international legally binding treaty on AI, called the "<a It was adopted by the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, and other signatories.<sup about="#mwt1329" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-375" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-375&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-375" id="mwCaU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCaY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCac">[</span>356<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCag">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCak">In a 2022 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipsos" title="Ipsos" id="mwCao">Ipsos</a> survey, attitudes towards AI varied greatly by country; 78% of Chinese citizens, but only 35% of Americans, agreed that "products and services using AI have more benefits than drawbacks".<sup about="#mwt1330" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEVincent2023_368-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEVincent2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEVincent2023-368&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Vincent&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVincent2023-368" id="mwCas"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCaw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCa0">[</span>349<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCa4">]</span></span></a></sup> A 2023 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters" title="Reuters" id="mwCa8">Reuters</a>/Ipsos poll found that 61% of Americans agree, and 22% disagree, that AI poses risks to humanity.<sup about="#mwt1333" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwards2023_376-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" id="mwCbM">]</span></span></a></sup> In a 2023 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News" title="Fox News" id="mwCbQ">Fox News</a> poll, 35% of Americans thought it "very important", and an additional 41% thought it "somewhat important", for the federal government to regulate AI, versus 13% responding "not very important" and 8% responding "not at all important".<sup data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEKasperowicz2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEKasperowicz2023-377&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Kasperowicz&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKasperowicz2023-377" id="mwCbU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCbY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCbc">[</span>358<span class="cite-bracket"
