<p id="mwCb0">In November 2023, the first global <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_Safety_Summit_2023" title="AI Safety Summit 2023" id="mwCb4">AI Safety Summit</a> was held in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bletchley_Park" title="Bletchley Park" id="mwCb8">Bletchley Park</a> in the UK to discuss the near and far term risks of AI and the possibility of mandatory and voluntary regulatory frameworks.<sup about="#mwt1344" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-379" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-379&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-379" id="mwCcA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCcE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcI">[</span>360<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcM">]</span></span></a></sup> 28 countries including the United States, China, and the European Union issued a declaration at the start of the summit, calling for international co-operation to manage the challenges and risks of artificial intelligence.<sup about="#mwt1347" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-380" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-380&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-380" id="mwCcQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCcU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcY">[</span>361<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1350" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-381" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-381&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-381" id="mwCcg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCck"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCco">[</span>362<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCcs">]</span></span></a></sup> In May 2024 at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_Seoul_Summit_2024" title="AI Seoul Summit 2024" id="mwCcw">AI Seoul Summit</a>, 16 global AI tech companies agreed to safety commitments on the development of AI.<sup about="#mwt1353" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-382" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-382&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-382" id="mwCc0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCc4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCc8">[</span>363<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCdA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1356" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-383" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-383&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-383" id="mwCdE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCdI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCdM">[</span>364<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCdQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCdU">In March 2026, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations" id="mwCdY">United Nations</a> convened the inaugural meeting of the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, a 40-member expert body established under the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Digital_Compact" title="Global Digital Compact" id="mwCdc">Global Digital Compact</a> to produce annual evidence-based reports on AI's societal impacts.<sup about="#mwt1359" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-384" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-384&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-384" id="mwCdg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCdk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCdo">[</span>365<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCds">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="51" id="mwCdw" aria-labelledby="History"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="History">History</h2></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1360" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCd0" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;History of artificial intelligence&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1361" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1360" id="mwCd4">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_artificial_intelligence" title="History of artificial intelligence">History of artificial intelligence</a></div>

<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1362" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCd8" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;For timeline&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:For_timeline&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1363" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1362" id="mwCeA">For a chronological guide, see <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Timeline of artificial intelligence">Timeline of artificial intelligence</a>.</div>

<!-- DON'T INCLUDE HISTORICAL PRECURSORS (THEY BELONG TO THE SEPARATE 'HISTORY OF AI' ARTICLE) -->
<!-- MAJOR INTELLECTUAL PRECURSORS: LOGIC, THEORY OF COMPUTATION, CYBERNETICS, INFORMATION THEORY, NEUROBIOLOGY, SPECULATION: Antiquity &#x2D; 1955 -->
<p id="mwCe0">The study of mechanical or "formal" reasoning began with philosophers and mathematicians in antiquity. The study of logic led directly to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Turing" title="Alan Turing" id="mwCe4">Alan Turing</a>'s <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_computation" title="Theory of computation" id="mwCe8">theory of computation</a>, which suggested that a machine, by shuffling symbols as simple as "0" and "1", could simulate any conceivable form of mathematical reasoning.<sup about="#mwt1368" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20219_386-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20219&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20219-386&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;9&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20219-386" id="mwCfA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCfE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCfI">[</span>367<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCfM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1387" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Clarendon_Press-2004_387-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Clarendon Press-2004&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Clarendon_Press-2004-387" id="mwCfQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCfU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCfY">[</span>368<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCfc">]</span></span></a></sup> This, along with concurrent discoveries in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybernetics" title="Cybernetics" id="mwCfg">cybernetics</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_theory" title="Information theory" id="mwCfk">information theory</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurobiology" title="Neurobiology" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCfo">neurobiology</a>, led researchers to consider the possibility of building an "electronic brain".<sup about="#mwt1371" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-389" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-389&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;\&quot;Electronic brain\&quot; was the term used by the press around this time.{{Sfn|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=9}}&lt;ref&gt;{{Cite web |title=Google books ngram |url=https://books.google.com/ngrams/graph?content=electronic+brain&amp;year_start=1930&amp;year_end=2019&amp;corpus=en-2019&amp;smoothing=3 |access-date=5 October 2024 |archive-date=5 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241005170209/https://books.google.com/ngrams/graph?content=electronic+brain&amp;year_start=1930&amp;year_end=2019&amp;corpus=en-2019&amp;smoothing=3 |url-status=live}}&lt;/ref&gt;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-389" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCfs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCfw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCf0">[</span>t<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCf4">]</span></span></a></sup> They developed several areas of research that would become part of AI,<sup about="#mwt1392" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-390" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-390&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-390" id="mwCf8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCgA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgE">[</span>370<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgI">]</span></span></a></sup> such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Sturgis_McCulloch" title="Warren Sturgis McCulloch" id="mwCgM">McCulloch</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Pitts" title="Walter Pitts" id="mwCgQ">Pitts</a> design for "artificial neurons" in 1943,<sup about="#mwt1384" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202117_130-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202117&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202117-130&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;17&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202117-130" id="mwCgU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCgY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgc">[</span>120<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCgg">]</span></span></a></sup> and Turing's influential 1950 paper '<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computing_Machinery_and_Intelligence" title="Computing Machinery and Intelligence" id="mwCgk">Computing Machinery and Intelligence</a>', which introduced the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_test" title="Turing test" id="mwCgo">Turing test</a> and showed that "machine intelligence" was plausible.<sup about="#mwt1393" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Turing_391-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Turing&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Turing-391" id="mwCgs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCgw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCg0">[</span>371<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCg4">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1396" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Clarendon_Press-2004_387-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Clarendon Press-2004&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Clarendon_Press-2004-387&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Clarendon_Press-2004-387" id="mwCg8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwChA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChE">[</span>368<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChI">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- 1956&#x2D;1974 -->
<p id="mwChM">The field of AI research was founded at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartmouth_workshop" title="Dartmouth workshop" id="mwChQ">a workshop</a> at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartmouth_College" title="Dartmouth College" id="mwChU">Dartmouth College</a> in 1956.<sup about="#mwt1397" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-393" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-393&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Daniel Crevier wrote, \&quot;the conference is generally recognized as the official birthdate of the new science.\&quot;{{Sfnp|Crevier|1993|pp=47–49}} [[Stuart J. Russell|Russell]] and [[Norvig]] called the conference \&quot;the inception of artificial intelligence.\&quot;{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=17}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-393" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwChY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwChc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChg">[</span>u<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChk">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1425" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Dartmouth_workshop_6-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Dartmouth workshop&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Dartmouth_workshop-6&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Dartmouth_workshop-6" id="mwCho"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwChs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwChw">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCh0">]</span></span></a></sup> The first AI program, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic_Theorist" title="Logic Theorist" id="mwCh4">Logic Theorist</a>, was presented at the workshop, created by future Turing Award winner <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Newell" title="Allen Newell" id="mwCh8">Allen Newell</a> and future Nobel Laureate <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_A._Simon" title="Herbert A. Simon" id="mwCiA">Herbert A. Simon</a>, in collaboration with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff_Shaw" title="Cliff Shaw" id="mwCiE">J. C. Shaw</a>. Many of the workshop attendees became the leaders of AI research in the 1960s.<sup about="#mwt1406" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-395" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-395&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Stuart J. Russell|Russell]] and [[Norvig]] wrote \&quot;for the next 20 years the field would be dominated by these people and their students.\&quot;{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2003|p=17}}\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-395" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCiI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCiM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCiQ">[</span>v<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCiU">]</span></span></a></sup> They and their students produced programs that the press described as "astonishing":<sup about="#mwt1412" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-397" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-397&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Stuart J. Russell|Russell]] and [[Norvig]] wrote, \&quot;it was astonishing whenever a computer did anything kind of smartish\&quot;.{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2003|p=18}}\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-397" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCiY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCic"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCig">[</span>w<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCik">]</span></span></a></sup> computers were learning <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkers" title="Checkers" id="mwCio">checkers</a> strategies, solving word problems in algebra, proving <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theorem" title="Theorem" id="mwCis">logical theorems</a> and speaking English.<sup about="#mwt1418" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-398" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-398&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;The programs described are [[Arthur Samuel (computer scientist)|Arthur Samuel]]'s checkers program for the [[IBM 701]], [[Daniel Bobrow]]'s [[STUDENT]], [[Allen Newell|Newell]] and [[Herbert A. Simon|Simon]]'s [[Logic Theorist]] and [[Terry Winograd]]'s [[SHRDLU]].\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-398" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCiw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCi0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCi4">[</span>x<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCi8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1430" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Succ1_7-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Succ1&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Succ1-7&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Succ1-7" id="mwCjA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCjE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjI">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjM">]</span></span></a></sup> Artificial intelligence laboratories were set up at a number of British and U.S. universities in the latter 1950s and early 1960s.<sup about="#mwt1431" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Clarendon_Press-2004_387-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Clarendon Press-2004&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Clarendon_Press-2004-387" id="mwCjQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCjU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjY">[</span>368<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjc">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- Optimism of the 60s and first AI "winter": 1974 -->
<p id="mwCjg">Researchers in the 1960s and the 1970s were convinced that their methods would eventually succeed in creating a machine with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence" title="Artificial general intelligence" id="mwCjk">general intelligence</a> and considered this the goal of their field.<sup about="#mwt1432" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENewquist199486–86_399-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTENewquist199486–86&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTENewquist199486–86-399&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Newquist&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1994&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;86–86&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENewquist199486–86-399" id="mwCjo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCjs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCjw">[</span>375<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCj0">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1965 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_A._Simon" title="Herbert A. Simon" id="mwCj4">Herbert Simon</a> predicted, "machines will be capable, within twenty years, of doing any work a man can do".<sup about="#mwt1452" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-400" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-400&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-400" id="mwCj8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCkA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkE">[</span>376<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkI">]</span></span></a></sup>In 1967 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Minsky" title="Marvin Minsky" id="mwCkM">Marvin Minsky</a> agreed, writing that "within a generation<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwCkQ">&nbsp;</span>... the problem of creating 'artificial intelligence' will substantially be solved".<sup about="#mwt1455" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-401" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-401&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-401" id="mwCkU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCkY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkc">[</span>377<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkg">]</span></span></a></sup> They had, however, underestimated the difficulty of the problem.<sup about="#mwt1435" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-403" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-403&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Stuart J. Russell|Russell]] and [[Norvig]] wrote: \&quot;in almost all cases, these early systems failed on more difficult problems\&quot;.{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=21}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-403" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCkk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCko"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCks">[</span>y<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCkw">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1974, both the U.S. and British governments cut off exploratory research in response to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthill_report" title="Lighthill report" id="mwCk0">criticism</a> of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_James_Lighthill" title="Sir James Lighthill" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCk4">Sir James Lighthill</a><sup about="#mwt1441" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELighthill1973_404-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELighthill1973&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELighthill1973-404&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Lighthill&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1973&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELighthill1973-404" id="mwCk8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwClA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwClE">[</span>379<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwClI">]</span></span></a></sup> and ongoing pressure from the U.S. Congress to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansfield_Amendment" title="Mansfield Amendment" class="mw-redirect" id="mwClM">fund more productive projects</a>.<sup about="#mwt1444" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENRC1999212–213_405-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTENRC1999212–213&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTENRC1999212–213-405&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;NRC&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1999&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;212–213&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENRC1999212–213-405" id="mwClQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwClU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwClY">[</span>380<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwClc">]</span></span></a></sup> Minsky and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papert" title="Papert" class="mw-redirect" id="mwClg">Papert</a>'s book <i id="mwClk"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptrons_(book)" title="Perceptrons (book)" id="mwClo">Perceptrons</a></i> was understood as proving that <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_networks" title="Artificial neural networks" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCls">artificial neural networks</a> would never be useful for solving real-world tasks, thus discrediting the approach altogether.<sup about="#mwt1447" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202122_406-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202122&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202122-406&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;22&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202122-406" id="mwClw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCl0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCl4">[</span>381<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCl8">]</span></span></a></sup> The "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_winter" title="AI winter" id="mwCmA">AI winter</a>", a period when obtaining funding for AI projects was difficult, followed.<sup about="#mwt1461" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-First_AI_Winter_9-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;First AI Winter&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-First_AI_Winter-9&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-First_AI_Winter-9" id="mwCmE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCmI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCmM">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCmQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- 1980s and second AI winter -->
<p id="mwCmU">In the early 1980s, AI research was revived by the commercial success of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expert_system" title="Expert system" id="mwCmY">expert systems</a>,<sup about="#mwt1468" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-407" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-407&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-407" id="mwCmc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCmg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCmk">[</span>382<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCmo">]</span></span></a></sup> a form of AI program that simulated the knowledge and analytical skills of human experts. By 1985, the market for AI had reached over a billion dollars. At the same time, Japan's <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_generation_computer" title="Fifth generation computer" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCms">fifth generation computer</a> project inspired the U.S. and British governments to restore funding for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_research" title="Academic research" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCmw">academic research</a>.<sup about="#mwt1474" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Fund01_8-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Fund01&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Fund01-8&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Fund01-8" id="mwCm0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCm4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCm8">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCnA">]</span></span></a></sup> However, beginning with the collapse of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisp_Machine" title="Lisp Machine" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCnE">Lisp Machine</a> market in 1987, AI once again fell into disrepute, and a second, longer-lasting winter began.<sup about="#mwt1480" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Second_AI_Winter_10-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Second AI Winter&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Second_AI_Winter-10&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Second_AI_Winter-10" id="mwCnI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCnM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCnQ">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCnU">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- Embodied robotics, uncertain reasoning, and connectionism in the 1980s -->
<p id="mwCnY">Up to this point, most of AI's funding had gone to projects that used high-level <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_AI" title="Symbolic AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCnc">symbols</a> to represent <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_objects" title="Mental objects" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCng">mental objects</a> like plans, goals, beliefs, and known facts. In the 1980s, some researchers began to doubt that this approach would be able to imitate all the processes of human cognition, especially <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_perception" title="Machine perception" id="mwCnk">perception</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotics" title="Robotics" id="mwCno">robotics</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning" id="mwCns">learning</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattern_recognition" title="Pattern recognition" id="mwCnw">pattern recognition</a>,<sup about="#mwt1481" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202124_408-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202124&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202124-408&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;24&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202124-408" id="mwCn0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCn4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCn8">[</span>383<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCoA">]</span></span></a></sup> and began to look into "sub-symbolic" approaches.<sup about="#mwt1484" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENilsson19987_409-0" rel="dc:references" href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENilsson19987-409" id="mwCoE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCoI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCoM">[</span>384<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCoQ">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Brooks" title="Rodney Brooks" id="mwCoU">Rodney Brooks</a> rejected "representation" in general and focussed directly on engineering machines that move and survive.<sup about="#mwt1487" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-414" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" mind|Embodied]] approaches to AI{{Sfnp|McCorduck|2004|pp=454–462}} were championed by [[Hans Moravec]]{{Sfnp|Moravec|1988}} and [[Rodney Brooks]]{{Sfnp|Brooks|1990}} and went by many names: [[Nouvelle AI]].{{Sfnp|Brooks|1990}} [[Developmental robotics]].&lt;ref&gt;[[Developmental robotics]]: {{Harvtxt|Weng|McClelland|Pentland|Sporns|2001}}, {{Harvtxt|Lungarella|Metta|Pfeifer|Sandini|2003}}, data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202125&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202125-415&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;25&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a id="mwCpM">]</span></span></a></sup> But the most important development was the revival of "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connectionism" title="Connectionism" id="mwCpQ">connectionism</a>", including neural network research, by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton" title="Geoffrey Hinton" id="mwCpU">Geoffrey Hinton</a> and others.<sup about="#mwt1518" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-416" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-416&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-416" id="mwCpY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCpc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCpg">[</span>390<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCpk">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1990, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yann_LeCun" title="Yann LeCun" id="mwCpo">Yann LeCun</a> successfully showed that <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convolutional_neural_networks" title="Convolutional neural networks" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCps">convolutional neural networks</a> can recognise handwritten digits, the first of many successful applications of neural networks.<sup about="#mwt1512" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202126_417-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202126&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202126-417&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;26&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202126-417" id="mwCpw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCp0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCp4">[</span>391<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCp8">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- 1990s: narrow, formal AI and its detractors -->
<p id="mwCqA">AI gradually restored its reputation in the late 1990s and early 21st century by exploiting formal mathematical methods and by finding specific solutions to specific problems. This "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrow_AI" title="Narrow AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCqE">narrow</a>" and "formal" focus allowed researchers to produce verifiable results and collaborate with other fields (such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistics" title="Statistics" id="mwCqI">statistics</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics" title="Economics" id="mwCqM">economics</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_optimization" title="Mathematical optimization" id="mwCqQ">mathematics</a>).<sup about="#mwt1521" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Formal_and_narrow_methods_adopted_in_the_1990s_418-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Formal and narrow methods adopted in the 1990s&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Formal_and_narrow_methods_adopted_in_the_1990s-418&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Formal_and_narrow_methods_adopted_in_the_1990s-418" id="mwCqU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCqY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCqc">[</span>392<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCqg">]</span></span></a></sup> By 2000, solutions developed by AI researchers were being widely used, although in the 1990s they were rarely described as "artificial intelligence" (a tendency known as the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_effect" title="AI effect" id="mwCqk">AI effect</a>).<sup about="#mwt1525" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-419" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-419&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-419" id="mwCqo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCqs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCqw">[</span>393<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCq0">]</span></span></a></sup>
However, several academic researchers became concerned that AI was no longer pursuing its original goal of creating versatile, fully intelligent machines. Beginning around 2002, they founded the subfield of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence" title="Artificial general intelligence" id="mwCq4">artificial general intelligence</a> (or "AGI"), which had several well-funded institutions by the 2010s.<sup about="#mwt1526" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Artificial_general_intelligence_80-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Artificial general intelligence&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Artificial_general_intelligence-80" id="mwCq8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCrA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrE">[</span>72<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrI">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!--DEEP LEARNING BOOM 2012–present-->
<p id="mwCrM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning" title="Deep learning" id="mwCrQ">Deep learning</a> began to dominate industry benchmarks in 2012 and was adopted throughout the field.<sup about="#mwt1530" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Deep_learning_revolution_11-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Deep learning revolution&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Deep_learning_revolution-11&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Deep_learning_revolution-11" id="mwCrU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCrY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrc">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrg">]</span></span></a></sup>
For many specific tasks, other methods were abandoned.<sup about="#mwt1531" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-421" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-421&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Matteo Wong wrote in ''[[The Atlantic]]'': \&quot;Whereas for decades, computer-science fields such as natural-language processing, computer vision, and robotics used extremely different methods, now they all use a programming method called \&quot;deep learning\&quot;. As a result, their code and approaches have become more similar, and their models are easier to integrate into one another.\&quot;{{Sfnp|Wong|2023}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-421" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCrk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCro"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrs">[</span>aa<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCrw">]</span></span></a></sup>
Deep learning's success was based on both hardware improvements (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moore's_law" title="Moore's law" id="mwCr0">faster computers</a>,<sup about="#mwt1544" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-422" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-422&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-422" id="mwCr4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCr8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCsA">[</span>395<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCsE">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit" title="Graphics processing unit" id="mwCsI">graphics processing units</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing" title="Cloud computing" id="mwCsM">cloud computing</a><sup about="#mwt1537" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEClark2015b_423-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEClark2015b&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark2015b-423&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Clark&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2015b&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark2015b-423" id="mwCsQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCsU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCsY">[</span>396<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCsc">]</span></span></a></sup>) and access to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_data" title="Big data" id="mwCsg">large amounts of data</a><sup about="#mwt1546" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-424" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-424&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-424" id="mwCsk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCso"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCss">[</span>397<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCsw">]</span></span></a></sup> (including curated datasets,<sup about="#mwt1540" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEClark2015b_423-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEClark2015b&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark2015b-423&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Clark&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2015b&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark2015b-423" id="mwCs0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCs4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCs8">[</span>396<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCtA">]</span></span></a></sup> such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ImageNet" title="ImageNet" id="mwCtE">ImageNet</a>). Neural-network approaches also advanced <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing" title="Natural language processing" id="mwCtI">natural language processing</a>. In 2013, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word2vec" title="Word2vec" id="mwCtM">word2vec</a> introduced efficient methods for learning distributed <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_embedding" title="Word embedding" id="mwCtQ">word representations</a>.<sup about="#mwt1549" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Apidianaki2023_425-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Apidianaki2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Apidianaki2023-425&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Apidianaki2023-425" id="mwCtU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCtY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCtc">[</span>398<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCtg">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2014–2015, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seq2seq" title="Seq2seq" id="mwCtk">sequence-to-sequence</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_(machine_learning)" title="Attention (machine learning)" id="mwCto">attention</a> mechanisms advanced neural machine translation.<sup about="#mwt1552" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-LeCunBengioHinton2015_426-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;LeCunBengioHinton2015&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-LeCunBengioHinton2015-426&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-LeCunBengioHinton2015-426" id="mwCts"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCtw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCt0">[</span>399<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCt4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwCt8">Deep learning's success led to an enormous increase in interest and funding in AI.<sup about="#mwt1553" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-427" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-427&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Jack Clark wrote in [[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]]: \&quot;After a half-decade of quiet breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, 2015 has been a landmark year. Computers are smarter and learning faster than ever\&quot;, and noted that the number of software projects that use machine learning at [[Google]] increased from a \&quot;sporadic usage\&quot; in 2012 to more than 2,700 projects in 2015.{{Sfnp|Clark|2015b}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-427" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwCuA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCuE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCuI">[</span>ab<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCuM">]</span></span></a></sup> The amount of machine learning research (measured by total publications) increased by 50% in the years 2015–2019.<sup about="#mwt1559" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEUNESCO2021_370-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEUNESCO2021&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEUNESCO2021-370&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;UNESCO&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUNESCO2021-370" id="mwCuQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCuU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCuY">[</span>351<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCuc">]</span></span></a></sup></p><!-- ALIGNMENT PROBLEM -->

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCug"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20250202_&quot;AI&quot;_(search_term)_on_Google_Trends.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwCuk"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20250202_&quot;AI&quot;_(search_term)_on_Google_Trends.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/20250202_%22AI%22_%28search_term%29_on_Google_Trends.svg/250px-20250202_%22AI%22_%28search_term%29_on_Google_Trends.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/20250202_%22AI%22_%28search_term%29_on_Google_Trends.svg/500px-20250202_%22AI%22_%28search_term%29_on_Google_Trends.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="750" data-file-type="drawing" height="188" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwCuo"></a><figcaption id="mwCus">The number of Google searches for the term "AI" accelerated in 2022.</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwCuw">In 2016, issues of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithmic_fairness" title="Algorithmic fairness" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCu0">fairness</a> and the misuse of technology were catapulted into centre stage at machine learning conferences, publications vastly increased, funding became available, and many researchers re-focussed their careers on these issues. The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_alignment" title="AI alignment" id="mwCu4">alignment problem</a> became a serious field of academic study.<sup about="#mwt1562" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian202067,_73_347-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian202067, 73&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202067,_73-347&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Christian&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2020&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;67, 73&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202067,_73-347" id="mwCu8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCvA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCvE">[</span>328<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCvI">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<!-- AI Boom 2020–present -->
<p id="mwCvM">In 2015, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlphaGo" title="AlphaGo" id="mwCvQ">AlphaGo</a>, developed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepMind" title="DeepMind" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCvU">DeepMind</a>, beat the world champion <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_player" title="Go player" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCvY">Go player</a>. The program taught only the game's rules and developed a strategy by itself. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPT-3" title="GPT-3" id="mwCvc">GPT-3</a> is a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model" title="Large language model" id="mwCvg">large language model</a> that was released in 2020 by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI" title="OpenAI" id="mwCvk">OpenAI</a> and is capable of generating high-quality human-like text.<sup about="#mwt1573" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-428" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-428&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-428" id="mwCvo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCvs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCvw">[</span>400<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCv0">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChatGPT" title="ChatGPT" id="mwCv4">ChatGPT</a>, launched on 30 November 2022, became the fastest-growing consumer software application in history, gaining over 100 million users in two months.<sup about="#mwt1576" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-429" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-429&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-429" id="mwCv8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCwA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCwE">[</span>401<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCwI">]</span></span></a></sup> It marked what is widely regarded as AI's breakout year, bringing it into the public consciousness.<sup about="#mwt1579" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-430" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-430&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-430" id="mwCwM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCwQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCwU">[</span>402<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCwY">]</span></span></a></sup> These programs, and others, inspired an aggressive <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_boom" title="AI boom" id="mwCwc">AI boom</a>, where large companies began investing billions of dollars in AI research. According to AI Impacts, about US$50 billion annually was invested in "AI" around 2022 in the U.S. alone and about 20% of the new U.S. computer science PhD graduates have specialised in "AI".<sup about="#mwt1565" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEDiFeliciantonio2023_431-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEDiFeliciantonio2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEDiFeliciantonio2023-431&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;DiFeliciantonio&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDiFeliciantonio2023-431" id="mwCwg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCwk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCwo">[</span>403<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCws">]</span></span></a></sup> About 800,000 "AI"-related U.S. job openings existed in 2022.<sup about="#mwt1568" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGoswami2023_432-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEGoswami2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoswami2023-432&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Goswami&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2023&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoswami2023-432" id="mwCww"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCw0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCw4">[</span>404<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCw8">]</span></span></a></sup> According to PitchBook research, 22% of newly funded <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Startups" title="Startups" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCxA">startups</a> in 2024 claimed to be AI companies.<sup about="#mwt1582" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-433" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-433&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-433" id="mwCxE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCxI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCxM">[</span>405<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCxQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="52" id="mwCxU" aria-labelledby="Philosophy"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Philosophy">Philosophy</h2></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1583" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCxY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Philosophy of artificial intelligence&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1584" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1583" id="mwCxc">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Philosophy of artificial intelligence">Philosophy of artificial intelligence</a></div>

<p id="mwCxg">Philosophical debates have historically sought to determine the nature of intelligence and how to make intelligent machines.<sup about="#mwt1587" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-434" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-434&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-434" id="mwCxk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCxo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCxs">[</span>406<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCxw">]</span></span></a></sup> Another major focus has been whether machines can be conscious, and the associated ethical implications.<sup about="#mwt1590" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Jarow-2024_435-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Jarow-2024&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Jarow-2024-435&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Jarow-2024-435" id="mwCx0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCx4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCx8">[</span>407<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCyA">]</span></span></a></sup> Many other topics in philosophy are relevant to AI, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistemology" title="Epistemology" id="mwCyE">epistemology</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_will" title="Free will" id="mwCyI">free will</a>.<sup about="#mwt1593" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-436" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-436&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-436" id="mwCyM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCyQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCyU">[</span>408<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCyY">]</span></span></a></sup> Rapid advancements have intensified public discussions on the philosophy and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethics_of_AI" title="Ethics of AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCyc">ethics of AI</a>.<sup about="#mwt1594" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Jarow-2024_435-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Jarow-2024&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Jarow-2024-435" id="mwCyg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCyk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCyo">[</span>407<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCys">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="53" id="mwCyw" aria-labelledby="Defining_artificial_intelligence"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Defining_artificial_intelligence">Defining artificial intelligence</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1595" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwCy0" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Synthetic intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Intelligent agent&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Artificial mind (disambiguation){{!}}Artificial mind&quot;},&quot;4&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Virtual intelligence&quot;},&quot;5&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Dartmouth workshop&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1596" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1595" id="mwCy4">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_intelligence" title="Synthetic intelligence">Synthetic intelligence</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligent_agent" title="Intelligent agent">Intelligent agent</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_mind_(disambiguation)" title="Artificial mind (disambiguation)" class="mw-redirect mw-disambig">Artificial mind</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_intelligence" title="Virtual intelligence">Virtual intelligence</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartmouth_workshop" title="Dartmouth workshop">Dartmouth workshop</a></div>

<p id="mwCy8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Turing" title="Alan Turing" id="mwCzA">Alan Turing</a> investigated whether machines can show intelligent behaviour and think. In 1950, he proposed the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_test" title="Turing test" id="mwCzE">Turing test</a>, which measures the ability of a machine to simulate human conversation.<sup about="#mwt1602" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-437" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-437&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-437" id="mwCzI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCzM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCzQ">[</span>409<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCzU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1608" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Turing_391-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Turing&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Turing-391&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Turing-391" id="mwCzY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCzc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCzg">[</span>371<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCzk">]</span></span></a></sup> Since we can only observe the behaviour of the machine, it does not matter if it is "actually" thinking or literally has a "mind". Turing notes that <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem_of_other_minds" title="Problem of other minds" id="mwCzo">we can not determine these things about other people</a> but "it is usual to have a polite convention that everyone thinks."<sup about="#mwt1597" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTETuring1950Under_&quot;The_Argument_from_Consciousness&quot;_438-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTETuring1950Under \&quot;The Argument from Consciousness\&quot;&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTETuring1950Under_\&quot;The_Argument_from_Consciousness\&quot;-438&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Turing&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1950&quot;},&quot;loc&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Under \&quot;The Argument from Consciousness\&quot;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTETuring1950Under_&quot;The_Argument_from_Consciousness&quot;-438" id="mwCzs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCzw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCz0">[</span>410<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCz4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwCz8"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Weakness_of_Turing_test_1.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwC0A"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Weakness_of_Turing_test_1.svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Weakness_of_Turing_test_1.svg/250px-Weakness_of_Turing_test_1.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Weakness_of_Turing_test_1.svg/500px-Weakness_of_Turing_test_1.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="433" data-file-height="316" data-file-type="drawing" height="182" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwC0E"></a><figcaption id="mwC0I">The Turing test can provide some evidence of intelligence, but it penalises non-human intelligent behaviour.<sup about="#mwt1611" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-439" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-439&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-439" id="mwC0M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC0Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC0U">[</span>411<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC0Y">]</span></span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwC0c"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_J._Russell" title="Stuart J. Russell" id="mwC0g">Russell</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norvig" title="Norvig" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC0k">Norvig</a> agree with Turing that intelligence must be defined in terms of external behaviour, not internal structure.<sup about="#mwt1612" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4_1-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4-1&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1–4&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4-1" id="mwC0o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC0s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC0w">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC00">]</span></span></a></sup> However, they are critical that the test requires the machine to imitate humans. "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeronautics" title="Aeronautics" id="mwC04">Aeronautical engineering</a> texts", they wrote, "do not define the goal of their field as making 'machines that fly so exactly like <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigeon" title="Pigeon" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC08">pigeons</a> that they can fool other pigeons.<span style="padding-right:.15em;" about="#mwt1615" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwC1A" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;' \&quot;&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:'_\&quot;&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}">'</span><span about="#mwt1615">"</span><sup about="#mwt1616" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20213_440-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20213&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20213-440&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;3&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20213-440" id="mwC1E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC1I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1M">[</span>412<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1Q">]</span></span></a></sup> AI founder <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCarthy_(computer_scientist)" title="John McCarthy (computer scientist)" id="mwC1U">John McCarthy</a> agreed, writing that "Artificial intelligence is not, by definition, simulation of human intelligence".<sup about="#mwt1619" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMaker2006_441-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMaker2006&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaker2006-441&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Maker&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2006&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaker2006-441" id="mwC1Y"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC1c"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1g">[</span>413<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1k">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwC1o">McCarthy defines intelligence as "the computational part of the ability to achieve goals in the world".<sup about="#mwt1622" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMcCarthy1999_442-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMcCarthy1999&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCarthy1999-442&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;McCarthy&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1999&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCarthy1999-442" id="mwC1s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC1w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC10">[</span>414<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC14">]</span></span></a></sup> Another AI founder, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Minsky" title="Marvin Minsky" id="mwC18">Marvin Minsky</a>, similarly describes it as "the ability to solve hard problems".<sup about="#mwt1625" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMinsky1986_443-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMinsky1986&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMinsky1986-443&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Minsky&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1986&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMinsky1986-443" id="mwC2A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC2E"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC2I">[</span>415<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC2M">]</span></span></a></sup> <i id="mwC2Q"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence:_A_Modern_Approach" title="Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach" id="mwC2U">Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach</a></i> defines it as the study of agents that perceive their environment and take actions that maximise their chances of achieving defined goals.<sup about="#mwt1628" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4_1-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4-1&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1–4&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211–4-1" id="mwC2Y"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC2c"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC2g">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC2k">]</span></span></a></sup></p> 

<p id="mwC2o">The many differing definitions of AI have been critically analysed.<sup about="#mwt1633" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-444" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-444&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-444" id="mwC2s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC2w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC20">[</span>416<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC24">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1636" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-445" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-445&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-445" id="mwC28"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC3A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC3E">[</span>417<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC3I">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1639" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-446" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-446&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-446" id="mwC3M"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC3Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC3U">[</span>418<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC3Y">]</span></span></a></sup> During the 2020s AI boom, the term has been used as a marketing <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buzzword" title="Buzzword" id="mwC3c">buzzword</a> to promote products and services which do not use AI.<sup about="#mwt1642" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-447" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-447&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-447" id="mwC3g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC3k"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC3o">[</span>419<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC3s">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="54" id="mwC3w" aria-labelledby="Legal_definitions"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Legal_definitions">Legal definitions</h4></div>
<p id="mwC30">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Organization_for_Standardization" title="International Organization for Standardization" id="mwC34">International Organization for Standardization</a> describes an AI system as a "an engineered system that generates outputs such as content, forecasts, recommendations, or decisions for a given set of human‑defined objectives, and can operate with varying levels of automation".<sup about="#mwt1645" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-448" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-448&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-448" id="mwC38"><span
