class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC4A"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC4E">[</span>420<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC4I">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence_Act" title="Artificial Intelligence Act" id="mwC4M">EU AI Act</a> defines an AI system as "a machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy and that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments".<sup about="#mwt1648" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-449" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-449&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-449" id="mwC4Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC4U"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC4Y">[</span>421<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC4c">]</span></span></a></sup> In the United States, influential but non‑binding guidance such as the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Standards_and_Technology" title="National Institute of Standards and Technology" id="mwC4g">National Institute of Standards and Technology</a>'s AI Risk Management Framework describes an AI system as "an engineered or machine-based system that can, for a given set of objectives, generate outputs such as predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments. AI systems are designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy".<sup about="#mwt1651" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-450" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-450&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-450" id="mwC4k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC4o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC4s">[</span>422<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC4w">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="55" id="mwC40" aria-labelledby="Evaluating_approaches_to_AI"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Evaluating_approaches_to_AI">Evaluating approaches to AI</h3></div>

<p id="mwC44">No established unifying theory or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradigm" title="Paradigm" id="mwC48">paradigm</a> has guided AI research for most of its history.<sup about="#mwt1652" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-452" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-452&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;[[Nils Nilsson (researcher)|Nils Nilsson]] wrote in 1983: \&quot;Simply put, there is wide disagreement in the field about what AI is all about.\&quot;{{Sfnp|Nilsson|1983|p=10}}&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-452" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwC5A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC5E"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC5I">[</span>ac<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC5M">]</span></span></a></sup> The unprecedented success of statistical machine learning in the 2010s eclipsed all other approaches (so much so that some sources, especially in the business world, use the term "artificial intelligence" to mean "machine learning with neural networks"). This approach is mostly <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-symbolic" title="Sub-symbolic" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC5Q">sub-symbolic</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_computing" title="Soft computing" id="mwC5U">soft</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrow_AI" title="Narrow AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC5Y">narrow</a>.</p>

<section data-mw-section-id="56" id="mwC5c" aria-labelledby="Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Symbolic_AI_and_its_limits">Symbolic AI and its limits</h4></div>
<p id="mwC5g"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_AI" title="Symbolic AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC5k">Symbolic AI</a> (or "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GOFAI" title="GOFAI" id="mwC5o">GOFAI</a>")<sup about="#mwt1658" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHaugeland1985112–117_453-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHaugeland1985112–117&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaugeland1985112–117-453&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Haugeland&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1985&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;112–117&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaugeland1985112–117-453" id="mwC5s"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC5w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC50">[</span>424<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC54">]</span></span></a></sup> simulated the high-level conscious reasoning that people use when they solve puzzles, express legal reasoning and do mathematics. It was highly successful at some "intelligent" tasks such as algebra or IQ tests. In 1976, Newell and Simon proposed the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_symbol_systems_hypothesis" title="Physical symbol systems hypothesis" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC58">physical symbol systems hypothesis</a>: "A physical symbol system has the necessary and sufficient means of general intelligent action."<sup about="#mwt1664" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-454" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-454&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-454" id="mwC6A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC6E"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC6I">[</span>425<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC6M">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwC6Q">However, the symbolic approach failed on many tasks that humans solve easily, such as learning, recognising an object or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonsense_reasoning" title="Commonsense reasoning" id="mwC6U">commonsense reasoning</a>. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moravec's_paradox" title="Moravec's paradox" id="mwC6Y">Moravec's paradox</a> is the discovery that high-level "intelligent" tasks were easy for AI, but low level "instinctive" tasks were extremely difficult.<sup about="#mwt1674" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-455" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-455&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-455" id="mwC6c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC6g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC6k">[</span>426<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC6o">]</span></span></a></sup> Philosopher <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_Dreyfus" title="Hubert Dreyfus" id="mwC6s">Hubert Dreyfus</a> had <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreyfus'_critique_of_AI" title="Dreyfus' critique of AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC6w">argued</a> since the 1960s that human expertise depends on embodied, situational know-how that is not representable as explicit symbolic rules rather than conscious symbol manipulation, and on having a "feel" for the situation, rather than explicit symbolic knowledge.<sup about="#mwt1681" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-456" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-456&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-456" id="mwC60"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC64"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC68">[</span>427<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC7A">]</span></span></a></sup> Although his arguments had been ridiculed and ignored when they were first presented, eventually, AI research came to agree with him.<sup about="#mwt1665" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-458" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-458&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn\n&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Daniel Crevier wrote that \&quot;time has proven the accuracy and perceptiveness of some of Dreyfus's comments. Had he formulated them less aggressively, constructive actions they suggested might have been taken much earlier.\&quot;{{Sfnp|Crevier|1993|p=125}}\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-458" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwC7E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC7I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC7M">[</span>ad<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC7Q">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1682" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Psychological_evidence_of_the_prevalence_of_sub_17-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Psychological evidence of the prevalence of sub&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Psychological_evidence_of_the_prevalence_of_sub-17" id="mwC7U"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC7Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC7c">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC7g">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwC7k">The issue is not resolved: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-symbolic" title="Sub-symbolic" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC7o">sub-symbolic</a> reasoning can make many of the same inscrutable mistakes that human intuition does, such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithmic_bias" title="Algorithmic bias" id="mwC7s">algorithmic bias</a>. Critics such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noam_Chomsky" title="Noam Chomsky" id="mwC7w">Noam Chomsky</a> argue continuing research into symbolic AI will still be necessary to attain general intelligence,<sup about="#mwt1683" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTELangley2011_459-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTELangley2011&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTELangley2011-459&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Langley&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2011&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTELangley2011-459" id="mwC70"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC74"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC78">[</span>429<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC8A">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1686" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKatz2012_460-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEKatz2012&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEKatz2012-460&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Katz&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2012&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKatz2012-460" id="mwC8E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC8I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC8M">[</span>430<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC8Q">]</span></span></a></sup> in part because sub-symbolic AI is a move away from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explainable_AI" title="Explainable AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC8U">explainable AI</a>: it can be difficult or impossible to understand why a modern statistical AI program made a particular decision. The emerging field of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuro-symbolic_AI" title="Neuro-symbolic AI" id="mwC8Y">neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence</a> attempts to bridge the two approaches.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="57" id="mwC8c" aria-labelledby="Neat_vs._scruffy"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Neat_vs._scruffy">Neat vs. scruffy</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1689" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwC8g" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Neats and scruffies&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1690" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1689" id="mwC8k">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neats_and_scruffies" title="Neats and scruffies">Neats and scruffies</a></div>

<p id="mwC8o">"Neats" hope that intelligent behaviour is described using simple, elegant principles (such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic" title="Logic" id="mwC8s">logic</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimization" title="Optimization" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC8w">optimisation</a>). "Scruffies" expect that it necessarily requires solving a large number of unrelated problems. Neats defend their programs with theoretical rigour, scruffies rely mainly on incremental testing to see if they work. This issue was actively discussed in the 1970s and 1980s.<sup about="#mwt1700" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-461" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-461&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-461" id="mwC80"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC84"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC88">[</span>431<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC9A">]</span></span></a></sup> The rise of deep learning may represent a shift toward the scruffies.<sup about="#mwt1691" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202142_462-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202142&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202142-462&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;42&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig202142-462" id="mwC9E"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC9I"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC9M">[</span>432<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC9Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p> 

</section><section data-mw-section-id="58" id="mwC9U" aria-labelledby="Soft_vs._hard_computing"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Soft_vs._hard_computing">Soft vs. hard computing</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1701" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwC9Y" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Soft computing&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1702" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1701" id="mwC9c">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_computing" title="Soft computing">Soft computing</a></div>

<p id="mwC9g">Finding a provably correct or optimal solution is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intractability_(complexity)" title="Intractability (complexity)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC9k">intractable</a> for many important problems.<sup about="#mwt1703" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Intractability_and_efficiency_and_the_combinatorial_explosion_16-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Intractability and efficiency and the combinatorial explosion&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Intractability_and_efficiency_and_the_combinatorial_explosion-16" id="mwC9o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC9s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC9w">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC90">]</span></span></a></sup> Soft computing is a set of techniques, including <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_algorithms" title="Genetic algorithms" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC94">genetic algorithms</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuzzy_logic" title="Fuzzy logic" id="mwC98">fuzzy logic</a> and neural networks, that are tolerant of imprecision, uncertainty, partial truth and approximation. Soft computing was introduced in the late 1980s and most successful AI programs in the 21st century are examples of soft computing with neural networks.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="59" id="mwC-A" aria-labelledby="Narrow_vs._general_AI"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Narrow_vs._general_AI">Narrow vs. general AI</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1704" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwC-E" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Weak artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Artificial general intelligence&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1705" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1704" id="mwC-I">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weak_artificial_intelligence" title="Weak artificial intelligence">Weak artificial intelligence</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence" title="Artificial general intelligence">Artificial general intelligence</a></div>

<p id="mwC-M">AI researchers are divided as to whether to pursue the goals of artificial general intelligence and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superintelligence" title="Superintelligence" id="mwC-Q">superintelligence</a> directly or to solve as many specific problems as possible (narrow AI) in hopes these solutions will lead indirectly to the field's long-term goals.<sup about="#mwt1706" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPennachinGoertzel2007_463-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEPennachinGoertzel2007&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEPennachinGoertzel2007-463&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Pennachin&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Goertzel&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2007&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPennachinGoertzel2007-463" id="mwC-U"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC-Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC-c">[</span>433<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC-g">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1709" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERoberts2016_464-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERoberts2016&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts2016-464&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Roberts&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2016&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts2016-464" id="mwC-k"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC-o"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC-s">[</span>434<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC-w">]</span></span></a></sup> General intelligence is difficult to define and difficult to measure, and modern AI has had more verifiable successes by focusing on specific problems with specific solutions. The sub-field of artificial general intelligence studies this area exclusively.</p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="60" id="mwC-0" aria-labelledby="Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Machine_consciousness,_sentience,_and_mind"><span id="Machine_consciousness.2C_sentience.2C_and_mind" typeof="mw:FallbackId"></span>Machine consciousness, sentience, and mind</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1712" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwC-4" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Philosophy of artificial intelligence&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Artificial consciousness&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1713" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1712" id="mwC-8">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Philosophy of artificial intelligence">Philosophy of artificial intelligence</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_consciousness" title="Artificial consciousness">Artificial consciousness</a></div>

<p id="mwC_A">There is no settled consensus in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_mind" title="Philosophy of mind" id="mwC_E">philosophy of mind</a> on whether a machine can have a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mind" title="Mind" id="mwC_I">mind</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consciousness" title="Consciousness" id="mwC_M">consciousness</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subjective_character_of_experience" title="Subjective character of experience" id="mwC_Q">subjective experiences</a> in the same sense that human beings do. This issue considers the internal experiences of the machine, rather than its external behaviour. Mainstream AI research considers this issue irrelevant because it does not affect the goals of the field: to build machines that can solve problems using intelligence. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_J._Russell" title="Stuart J. Russell" id="mwC_U">Russell</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norvig" title="Norvig" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC_Y">Norvig</a> add that "[t]he additional project of making a machine conscious in exactly the way humans are is not one that we are equipped to take on."<sup about="#mwt1714" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021986_465-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021986&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021986-465&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;986&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig2021986-465" id="mwC_c"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC_g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC_k">[</span>435<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC_o">]</span></span></a></sup> However, the question has become central to the philosophy of mind. It is also typically the central question at issue in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_in_fiction" title="Artificial intelligence in fiction" id="mwC_s">artificial intelligence in fiction</a>.</p>

<section data-mw-section-id="61" id="mwC_w" aria-labelledby="Consciousness"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Consciousness">Consciousness</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1717" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwC_0" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Hard problem of consciousness&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Theory of mind&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1718" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1717" id="mwC_4">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_problem_of_consciousness" title="Hard problem of consciousness">Hard problem of consciousness</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_mind" title="Theory of mind">Theory of mind</a></div>

<p id="mwC_8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Chalmers" title="David Chalmers" id="mwDAA">David Chalmers</a> identified two problems in understanding the mind, which he named the "hard" and "easy" problems of consciousness.<sup about="#mwt1719" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChalmers1995_466-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChalmers1995&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChalmers1995-466&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Chalmers&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1995&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChalmers1995-466" id="mwDAE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDAI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDAM">[</span>436<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDAQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The easy problem is understanding how the brain processes signals, makes plans and controls behaviour. The hard problem is explaining how this <i id="mwDAU">feels</i> or why it should feel like anything at all, assuming we are right in thinking that it truly does feel like something (Dennett's consciousness illusionism says this is an illusion). While human <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_processing_(psychology)" title="Information processing (psychology)" id="mwDAY">information processing</a> is easy to explain, human <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subjective_experience" title="Subjective experience" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDAc">subjective experience</a> is difficult to explain. For example, it is easy to imagine a colour-blind person who has learned to identify which objects in their field of view are red, but it is not clear what would be required for the person to <i id="mwDAg">know what red looks like</i>.<sup about="#mwt1722" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEDennett1991_467-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEDennett1991&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEDennett1991-467&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Dennett&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1991&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDennett1991-467" id="mwDAk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDAo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDAs">[</span>437<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDAw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="62" id="mwDA0" aria-labelledby="Computationalism_and_functionalism"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Computationalism_and_functionalism">Computationalism and functionalism</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1725" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwDA4" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Computational theory of mind&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Functionalism (philosophy of mind)&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1726" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1725" id="mwDA8">Main articles: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_theory_of_mind" title="Computational theory of mind">Computational theory of mind</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functionalism_(philosophy_of_mind)" title="Functionalism (philosophy of mind)">Functionalism (philosophy of mind)</a></div>

<p id="mwDBA">Computationalism is the position in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_mind" title="Philosophy of mind" id="mwDBE">philosophy of mind</a> that the human mind is an information processing system and that thinking is a form of computing. Computationalism argues that the relationship between mind and body is similar or identical to the relationship between software and hardware and thus may be a solution to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mind–body_problem" title="Mind–body problem" id="mwDBI">mind–body problem</a>. This philosophical position was inspired by the work of AI researchers and cognitive scientists in the 1960s and was originally proposed by philosophers <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Fodor" title="Jerry Fodor" id="mwDBM">Jerry Fodor</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilary_Putnam" title="Hilary Putnam" id="mwDBQ">Hilary Putnam</a>.<sup about="#mwt1727" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHorst2005_468-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEHorst2005&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEHorst2005-468&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Horst&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2005&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHorst2005-468" id="mwDBU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDBY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDBc">[</span>438<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDBg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDBk">Philosopher <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Searle" title="John Searle" id="mwDBo">John Searle</a> characterised this position as "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strong_AI_hypothesis" title="Strong AI hypothesis" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDBs">strong AI</a>": "The appropriately programmed computer with the right inputs and outputs would thereby have a mind in exactly the same sense human beings have minds."<sup about="#mwt1730" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Searle's_strong_AI_472-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Searle's strong AI&quot;,&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Searle's_strong_AI-472&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Efn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Efn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;\&quot;Searle's strong AI\&quot;&quot;},&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Searle presented this definition of \&quot;Strong AI\&quot; in 1999.{{Sfnp|Searle|1999}} Searle's original formulation was \&quot;The appropriately programmed computer really is a mind, in the sense that computers given the right programs can be literally said to understand and have other cognitive states.\&quot;{{Sfnp|Searle|1980|p=1}} Strong AI is defined similarly by [[Stuart J. Russell|Russell]] and [[Norvig]]: \&quot;Strong AI – the assertion that machines that do so are ''actually'' consciously thinking (as opposed to ''simulating'' thinking).\&quot;{{Sfnp|Russell|Norvig|2021|p=1032}}\n&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-Searle's_strong_AI-472" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwDBw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDB0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDB4">[</span>ae<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDB8">]</span></span></a></sup> Searle challenges this claim with his <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_room" title="Chinese room" id="mwDCA">Chinese room</a> argument, which attempts to show that even a computer capable of perfectly simulating human behaviour would not have a mind.<sup about="#mwt1747" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-473" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-473&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-473" id="mwDCE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDCI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDCM">[</span>442<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDCQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="63" id="mwDCU" aria-labelledby="AI_welfare_and_rights"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="AI_welfare_and_rights">AI welfare and rights</h4></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1748" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwDCY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;See also&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:See_also&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Ethics of artificial intelligence#AI welfare&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1749" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1748" id="mwDCc">See also: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethics_of_artificial_intelligence#AI_welfare" title="Ethics of artificial intelligence">Ethics of artificial intelligence §<span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span>AI welfare</a></div>
<p id="mwDCg">It is difficult or impossible to reliably evaluate whether an advanced <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentient_AI" title="Sentient AI" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDCk">AI is sentient</a> (has the ability to feel), and if so, to what degree.<sup about="#mwt1752" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-474" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-474&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-474" id="mwDCo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDCs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDCw">[</span>443<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDC0">]</span></span></a></sup> But if there is a significant chance that a given machine can feel and suffer, then it may be entitled to certain rights or welfare protection measures, similarly to animals.<sup about="#mwt1755" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Thomson-2022_475-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Thomson-2022&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Thomson-2022-475&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Thomson-2022-475" id="mwDC4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDC8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDDA">[</span>444<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDDE">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1758" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Kateman-2023_476-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kateman-2023&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Kateman-2023-476&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Kateman-2023-476" id="mwDDI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDDM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDDQ">[</span>445<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDDU">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapience" title="Sapience" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDDY">Sapience</a> (a set of capacities related to high intelligence, such as discernment or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-awareness" title="Self-awareness" id="mwDDc">self-awareness</a>) may provide another moral basis for AI rights.<sup about="#mwt1759" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Thomson-2022_475-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Thomson-2022&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Thomson-2022-475" id="mwDDg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDDk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDDo">[</span>444<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDDs">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robot_rights" title="Robot rights" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDDw">Robot rights</a> are also sometimes proposed as a practical way to integrate autonomous agents into society.<sup about="#mwt1762" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-477" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-477&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-477" id="mwDD0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDD4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDD8">[</span>446<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDEA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDEE">In 2017, the European Union considered granting "electronic personhood" to some of the most capable AI systems. Similarly to the legal status of companies, it would have conferred rights but also responsibilities.<sup about="#mwt1765" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-478" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-478&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-478" id="mwDEI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDEM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDEQ">[</span>447<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDEU">]</span></span></a></sup> Critics argued in 2018 that granting rights to AI systems would downplay the importance of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights" title="Human rights" id="mwDEY">human rights</a>, and that legislation should focus on user needs rather than speculative futuristic scenarios. They also noted that robots lacked the autonomy to take part in society on their own.<sup about="#mwt1768" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-479" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-479&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-479" id="mwDEc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDEg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDEk">[</span>448<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDEo">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1771" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-480" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-480&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-480" id="mwDEs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDEw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDE0">[</span>449<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDE4">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDE8">Progress in AI increased interest in the topic. Proponents of AI welfare and rights often argue that AI sentience, if it emerges, would be particularly easy to deny. They warn that this may be a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moral_blindness" title="Moral blindness" id="mwDFA">moral blind spot</a> analogous to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery" title="Slavery" id="mwDFE">slavery</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory_farming" title="Factory farming" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDFI">factory farming</a>, which could lead to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suffering_risks" title="Suffering risks" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDFM">large-scale suffering</a> if sentient AI is created and carelessly exploited.<sup about="#mwt1772" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Kateman-2023_476-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kateman-2023&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Kateman-2023-476" id="mwDFQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDFU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDFY">[</span>445<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDFc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1773" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Thomson-2022_475-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Thomson-2022&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Thomson-2022-475" id="mwDFg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDFk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDFo">[</span>444<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDFs">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section></section><section data-mw-section-id="64" id="mwDFw" aria-labelledby="Future"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Future">Future</h2></div>
<section data-mw-section-id="65" id="mwDF0" aria-labelledby="Superintelligence_and_the_singularity"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Superintelligence_and_the_singularity">Superintelligence and the singularity</h3></div>

<p id="mwDF4">A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superintelligence" title="Superintelligence" id="mwDF8">superintelligence</a> is a hypothetical agent that would possess intelligence far surpassing that of the brightest and most gifted human mind.<sup about="#mwt1774" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERoberts2016_464-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERoberts2016&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts2016-464&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Roberts&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2016&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts2016-464" id="mwDGA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDGE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDGI">[</span>434<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDGM">]</span></span></a></sup> If research into <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence" title="Artificial general intelligence" id="mwDGQ">artificial general intelligence</a> produced sufficiently intelligent software, it might be able to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recursive_self-improvement" title="Recursive self-improvement" id="mwDGU">reprogram and improve itself</a>. The improved software would be even better at improving itself, leading to what <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I._J._Good" title="I. J. Good" id="mwDGY">I. J. Good</a> called an "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_explosion" title="Intelligence explosion" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDGc">intelligence explosion</a>" and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernor_Vinge" title="Vernor Vinge" id="mwDGg">Vernor Vinge</a> called a "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technological_singularity" title="Technological singularity" id="mwDGk">singularity</a>".<sup about="#mwt1782" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-481" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-481&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-481" id="mwDGo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDGs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDGw">[</span>450<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDG0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDG4">In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence:_A_Modern_Approach" title="Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach" id="mwDG8">Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach</a>, Russel and Norvig cast doubt on the possibility of a singularity, arguing that "so far, every technology has followed an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S-shaped_curve" title="S-shaped curve" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDHA">S-shaped curve</a>", and that "sometimes it is not possible to keep the growth going."<sup about="#mwt1783" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211005_482-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211005&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211005-482&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Russell&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Norvig&quot;},&quot;3&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2021&quot;},&quot;p&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1005&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211005-482" id="mwDHE"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDHI"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDHM">[</span>451<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDHQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="66" id="mwDHU" aria-labelledby="Transhumanism"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Transhumanism">Transhumanism</h3></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1786" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwDHY" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Transhumanism&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1787" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1786" id="mwDHc">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transhumanism" title="Transhumanism">Transhumanism</a></div>

<p id="mwDHg">Robot designer <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Moravec" title="Hans Moravec" id="mwDHk">Hans Moravec</a>, cyberneticist <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Warwick" title="Kevin Warwick" id="mwDHo">Kevin Warwick</a> and inventor <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Kurzweil" title="Ray Kurzweil" id="mwDHs">Ray Kurzweil</a> have predicted that humans and machines may merge in the future into <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyborg" title="Cyborg" id="mwDHw">cyborgs</a> that are more capable and powerful than either. This idea, called transhumanism, has roots in the writings of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldous_Huxley" title="Aldous Huxley" id="mwDH0">Aldous Huxley</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Ettinger" title="Robert Ettinger" id="mwDH4">Robert Ettinger</a>.<sup about="#mwt1791" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-483" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-483&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-483" id="mwDH8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDIA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDIE">[</span>452<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDII">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDIM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fredkin" title="Edward Fredkin" id="mwDIQ">Edward Fredkin</a> argues that "artificial intelligence is the next step in evolution", an idea first proposed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Butler_(novelist)" title="Samuel Butler (novelist)" id="mwDIU">Samuel Butler</a>'s "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_among_the_Machines" title="Darwin among the Machines" id="mwDIY">Darwin among the Machines</a>" as far back as 1863, and expanded upon by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Dyson_(science_historian)" title="George Dyson (science historian)" id="mwDIc">George Dyson</a> in his 1998 book <i id="mwDIg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darwin_Among_the_Machines#Evolution_of_Global_Intelligence" title="Darwin Among the Machines" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDIk">Darwin Among the Machines: The Evolution of Global Intelligence</a></i>.<sup about="#mwt1795" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-484" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-484&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-484" id="mwDIo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDIs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDIw">[</span>453<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDI0">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="67" id="mwDI4" aria-labelledby="In_fiction"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="In_fiction">In fiction</h2></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1796" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwDI8" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Main&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Main&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Artificial intelligence in fiction&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237" about="#mwt1797" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;templatestyles&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;Module:Hatnote/styles.css&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;extsrc&quot;:&quot;&quot;}}"></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt1796" id="mwDJA">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_in_fiction" title="Artificial intelligence in fiction">Artificial intelligence in fiction</a></div>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwDJE"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Capek_play.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwDJI"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Capek_play.jpg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Capek_play.jpg/330px-Capek_play.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/87/Capek_play.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled 2x" data-file-width="566" data-file-height="316" data-file-type="bitmap" height="167" width="300" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.2" id="mwDJM"></a><figcaption id="mwDJQ">The word "robot" itself was coined by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karel_Čapek" title="Karel Čapek" id="mwDJU">Karel Čapek</a> in his 1921 play <i id="mwDJY"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.U.R." title="R.U.R." id="mwDJc">R.U.R.</a></i>, the title standing for "Rossum's Universal Robots".</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwDJg">Thought-capable artificial beings have appeared as storytelling devices since antiquity,<sup about="#mwt1802" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-AI_in_myth_485-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;AI in myth&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-AI_in_myth-485&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-AI_in_myth-485" id="mwDJk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDJo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDJs">[</span>454<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDJw">]</span></span></a></sup> and have been a persistent theme in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction" title="Science fiction" id="mwDJ0">science fiction</a>.<sup about="#mwt1798" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMcCorduck2004340–400_486-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMcCorduck2004340–400&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCorduck2004340–400-486&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;McCorduck&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2004&quot;},&quot;pp&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;340–400&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCorduck2004340–400-486" id="mwDJ4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDJ8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDKA">[</span>455<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDKE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDKI">A common <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trope_(literature)" title="Trope (literature)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDKM">trope</a> in these works began with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Shelley" title="Mary Shelley" id="mwDKQ">Mary Shelley</a>'s <i id="mwDKU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankenstein" title="Frankenstein" id="mwDKY">Frankenstein</a></i>, where a human creation becomes a threat to its masters. This includes such works as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001:_A_Space_Odyssey_(novel)" title="2001: A Space Odyssey (novel)" id="mwDKc">Arthur C. Clarke's</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001:_A_Space_Odyssey" title="2001: A Space Odyssey" id="mwDKg">Stanley Kubrick's</a> <i id="mwDKk">2001: A Space Odyssey</i> (both 1968), with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HAL_9000" title="HAL 9000" id="mwDKo">HAL 9000</a>, the murderous computer in charge of the <i id="mwDKs"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_One" title="Discovery One" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDKw">Discovery One</a></i> spaceship, as well as <i id="mwDK0"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade_Runner" title="Blade Runner" id="mwDK4">Blade Runner</a></i> (1982), <i id="mwDK8"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Terminator" title="The Terminator" id="mwDLA">The Terminator</a></i> (1984) and <i id="mwDLE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix" title="The Matrix" id="mwDLI">The Matrix</a></i> (1999). In contrast, the rare loyal robots such as Gort from <i id="mwDLM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Day_the_Earth_Stood_Still" title="The Day the Earth Stood Still" id="mwDLQ">The Day the Earth Stood Still</a></i> (1951) and Bishop from <i id="mwDLU"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliens_(film)" title="Aliens (film)" id="mwDLY">Aliens</a></i> (1986) are less prominent in popular culture.<sup about="#mwt1803" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEButtazzo2001_487-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEButtazzo2001&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEButtazzo2001-487&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Buttazzo&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2001&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEButtazzo2001-487" id="mwDLc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDLg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDLk">[</span>456<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDLo">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDLs"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Asimov" title="Isaac Asimov" id="mwDLw">Isaac Asimov</a> introduced the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Laws_of_Robotics" title="Three Laws of Robotics" id="mwDL0">Three Laws of Robotics</a> in many stories, most notably with the "<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multivac" title="Multivac" id="mwDL4">Multivac</a>" super-intelligent computer. Asimov's laws are often brought up during lay discussions of machine ethics;<sup about="#mwt1806" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAnderson2008_488-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEAnderson2008&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson2008-488&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Anderson&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2008&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson2008-488" id="mwDL8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDMA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDME">[</span>457<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDMI">]</span></span></a></sup> while almost all artificial intelligence researchers are familiar with Asimov's laws through popular culture, they generally consider the laws useless for many reasons, one of which is their ambiguity.<sup about="#mwt1809" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMcCauley2007_489-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEMcCauley2007&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCauley2007-489&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;McCauley&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;2007&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCauley2007-489" id="mwDMM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDMQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDMU">[</span>458<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDMY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwDMc">Several works use AI to force us to confront the fundamental question of what makes us human, showing us artificial beings that have <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentience" title="Sentience" id="mwDMg">the ability to feel</a>, and thus to suffer. This appears in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karel_Čapek" title="Karel Čapek" id="mwDMk">Karel Čapek</a>'s <i id="mwDMo"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.U.R." title="R.U.R." id="mwDMs">R.U.R.</a></i>, the films <i id="mwDMw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.I._Artificial_Intelligence" title="A.I. Artificial Intelligence" id="mwDM0">A.I. Artificial Intelligence</a></i> and <i id="mwDM4"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex_Machina_(film)" title="Ex Machina (film)" id="mwDM8">Ex Machina</a></i>, as well as the novel <i id="mwDNA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do_Androids_Dream_of_Electric_Sheep%3F" title="Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?" id="mwDNE">Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?</a></i>, by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_K._Dick" title="Philip K. Dick" id="mwDNI">Philip K. Dick</a>. Dick considers the idea that our understanding of human subjectivity is altered by technology created with artificial intelligence.<sup about="#mwt1812" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGalvan1997_490-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEGalvan1997&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEGalvan1997-490&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Sfnp&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Sfnp&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Galvan&quot;},&quot;2&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;1997&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGalvan1997-490" id="mwDNM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDNQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDNU">[</span>459<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDNY">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<li about="#cite_note-38" id="cite_note-38" data-mw-footnote-number="f"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDTM"><a href="#cite_ref-38" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDTQ"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDTU">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-38" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">"Rational agent" is general term used in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics" title="Economics" id="mwDTY">economics</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy" title="Philosophy" id="mwDTc">philosophy</a> and theoretical artificial intelligence. <li about="#cite_note-138" id="cite_note-138" data-mw-footnote-number="l"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDa8"><a href="#cite_ref-138" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDbA"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDbE">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-138" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Hinton" title="Geoffrey Hinton" id="mwDbI">Geoffrey Hinton</a> said, of his work on neural networks in the 1990s, "our labeled datasets were thousands of times too small. [And] our computers were millions of times too slow."<sup about="#mwt485" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-137" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-137&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-137" id="mwDbM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDbQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDbU">[</span>126<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDbY">]</span></span></a></sup></span></li>
<li about="#cite_note-264" id="cite_note-264" data-mw-footnote-number="m"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDbc"><a href="#cite_ref-264" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDbg"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDbk">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-264" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">In statistics, a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bias_(statistics)" title="Bias (statistics)" id="mwDbo">bias</a> is a systematic error or deviation from the correct value. But in the context of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairness_(machine_learning)" title="Fairness (machine learning)" id="mwDbs">fairness</a>, it refers to a tendency in favour or against a certain group or individual characteristic, usually in a way that is considered unfair or harmful. A statistically unbiased AI system that produces disparate outcomes for different demographic groups may thus be viewed as biased in the ethical sense.<sup about="#mwt937" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Samuel-2022_263-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Samuel-2022&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-Samuel-2022-263" id="mwDbw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDb0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDb4">[</span>251<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDb8">]</span></span></a></sup></span></li>
<li about="#cite_note-275" id="cite_note-275" data-mw-footnote-number="n"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDcA"><a href="#cite_ref-275" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDcE"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDcI">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-275" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">Including <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Kleinberg" title="Jon Kleinberg" id="mwDcM">Jon Kleinberg</a> (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University" title="Cornell University" id="mwDcQ">Cornell University</a>), Sendhil Mullainathan (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago" title="University of Chicago" id="mwDcU">University of Chicago</a>), Cynthia Chouldechova (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Mellon" title="Carnegie Mellon" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDcY">Carnegie Mellon</a>) and Sam Corbett-Davis (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford" title="Stanford" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDcc">Stanford</a>)<sup about="#mwt975" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEChristian202067–70_274-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEChristian202067–70&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202067–70-274&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChristian202067–70-274" id="mwDcg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDck"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDco">[</span>261<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDcs">]</span></span></a></sup></span></li>
<li about="#cite_note-281" id="cite_note-281" data-mw-footnote-number="o"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDcw"><a href="#cite_ref-281" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDc0"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDc4">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-281" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">Moritz Hardt (a director at the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Planck_Institute_for_Intelligent_Systems" title="Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems" id="mwDc8">Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems</a>) argues that machine learning "is fundamentally the wrong tool for a lot of domains, where you're trying to design interventions and mechanisms that change the world."<sup about="#mwt992" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-280" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-280&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-280" id="mwDdA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDdE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDdI">[</span>266<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDdM">]</span></span></a></sup></span></li>

Computers are smarter and learning faster than ever", and noted that the number of software projects that use machine learning at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google" title="Google" id="mwDlc">Google</a> increased from a "sporadic usage" in 2012 to more than 2,700 projects in 2015.<sup about="#mwt1554" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEClark2015b_423-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTEClark2015b&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark2015b-423&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark2015b-423" id="mwDlg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDlk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDlo">[</span>396<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDls">]</span></span></a></sup></span></li>
<li about="#cite_note-452" id="cite_note-452" data-mw-footnote-number="ac"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDlw"><a href="#cite_ref-452" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDl0"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDl4">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-452" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nils_Nilsson_(researcher)" title="Nils Nilsson (researcher)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDl8">Nils Nilsson</a> wrote in 1983: "Simply put, there is wide disagreement in the field about what AI is all about."<sup about="#mwt1653" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTENilsson198310_451-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTENilsson198310&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTENilsson198310-451&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTENilsson198310-451" id="mwDmA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDmE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDmI">[</span>423<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDmM">]</span></span></a></sup></span></li>
<li about="#cite_note-458" id="cite_note-458" data-mw-footnote-number="ad"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDmQ"><a href="#cite_ref-458" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDmU"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDmY">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-458" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">Daniel Crevier wrote that "time has proven the accuracy and perceptiveness of some of Dreyfus's comments. Had he formulated them less aggressively, constructive actions they suggested might have been taken much earlier."<sup about="#mwt1666" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECrevier1993125_457-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTECrevier1993125&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTECrevier1993125-457&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrevier1993125-457" id="mwDmc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDmg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDmk">[</span>428<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDmo">]</span></span></a></sup>
</span></li>
<li about="#cite_note-Searle's_strong_AI-472" id="cite_note-Searle's_strong_AI-472" data-mw-footnote-number="ae"><span class="mw-cite-backlink" id="mwDms"><a href="#cite_ref-Searle's_strong_AI_472-0" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" rel="mw:referencedBy" id="mwDmw"><span class="mw-linkback-text" id="mwDm0">↑</span></a></span> <span id="mw-reference-text-cite_note-Searle's_strong_AI-472" class="mw-reference-text reference-text" data-mw-group="lower-alpha">Searle presented this definition of "Strong AI" in 1999.<sup about="#mwt1731" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESearle1999_469-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESearle1999&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESearle1999-469&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESearle1999-469" id="mwDm4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDm8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDnA">[</span>439<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDnE">]</span></span></a></sup> Searle's original formulation was "The appropriately programmed computer really is a mind, in the sense that computers given the right programs can be literally said to understand and have other cognitive states."<sup about="#mwt1733" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESearle19801_470-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTESearle19801&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTESearle19801-470&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESearle19801-470" id="mwDnI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDnM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDnQ">[</span>440<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDnU">]</span></span></a></sup> Strong AI is defined similarly by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_J._Russell" title="Stuart J. Russell" id="mwDnY">Russell</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norvig" title="Norvig" class="mw-redirect" id="mwDnc">Norvig</a>: "Strong AI – the assertion that machines that do so are <i id="mwDng">actually</i> consciously thinking (as opposed to <i id="mwDnk">simulating</i> thinking)."<sup about="#mwt1735" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211032_471-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;name&quot;:&quot;FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211032&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211032-471&quot;}}"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERussellNorvig20211032-471" id="mwDno"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDns"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDnw">[</span>441<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDn0">]</span></span></a></sup>
</span></li>
</ol></div></div>

Another common objection to anthropomorphism by design is that it is deceptive insofar as it would appear that in order to meet specific, e.g. emotional or social needs, AI must actually “fool” users by making them believe that they have the capacity to engage emotionally\&quot;&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><cite id="CITEREFSalles,_ArleenEvers,_KathinkaFarisco,_Michele2020" class="citation journal cs1 cs1-prop-long-vol" about="#mwt1144">Salles, Arleen; Evers, Kathinka; Farisco, Michele (2020). <a rel="mw:ExtLink nofollow" href="https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/21507740.2020.1740350" class="external text" id="mwGkI">"Anthropomorphism in AI"</a>. <i id="mwGkM">AJOB Neuroscience</i>. 2020 Vol 11 (2): <span class="nowrap" id="mwGkQ">88–</span>95. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doi_(identifier)" title="Doi (identifier)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwGkU">doi</a>:<a rel="mw:ExtLink nofollow" href="https://doi.org/10.1080%2F21507740.2020.1740350" class="external text" id="mwGkY">10.1080/21507740.2020.1740350</a>. <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PMID_(identifier)" title="PMID (identifier)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwGkc">PMID</a><span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwGkg">&nbsp;</span><a rel="mw:ExtLink nofollow" href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32228388" class="external text" id="mwGkk">32228388</a>. <q id="mwGko">An additional concern is that socialization with entities that are not truly social, even if designed to offer new tools for enriching users' emotional life and even if beneficial in some specific cases (for example, when enhancing the well-being of those who would otherwise be social outcasts) is not truly meaningful and it can only limitedly replace the richness of human interactions....
